questions.stem: A Service Catalog may include which of the following components?

options.text: Order Guides, Catalog Items, and Interceptors
Catalog Items, Asset Contracts, Task Surveys
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items

questions.explanation: A Service Catalog contains Record Producers (create task-based records from the catalog), Order Guides (bundle multiple related items into one request), and Catalog Items (individual orderable items/services). Exchange Rates, Calendars, Asset Contracts, and Task Surveys are not Service Catalog components.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements applies to a set of fields when they are coalesced during an import?

options.text: If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the information being imported
If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the system does not create a Transform Map
If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the system creates a new record
If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the information being imported

questions.explanation: When fields are coalesced during an import, they act as unique keys. If a match IS found using coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the imported data. If no match is found, a new record is created. Coalesce prevents duplicate records by identifying existing records to update rather than creating duplicates.

questions.stem: As it relates to ServiceNow reporting, which of the following statements describes what a metric can do?

options.text: A metric is a report gauge used on homepages to display real-time data
A metric is a time measurement used to report the effectiveness of workflows and SLAs
A metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of IT service management processes
A metric is a comparative measurement used to report the effectiveness of flows and SLAs.

questions.explanation: In ServiceNow reporting, a metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of IT service management processes. It tracks key measurements over time. A metric is not a report gauge (A), not just about time measurement for workflows/SLAs (B), and not specifically a comparative measurement (D).

questions.stem: The display sequence is controlled in a Service Catalog Item using which of the following?

options.text: The Default Value field in the Catalog Item form
The Sequence field in the Catalog Item form
The Order field in the Variable form
The Choice field in the Variable form

questions.explanation: The display sequence of catalog variables on a Service Catalog Item is controlled by the Order field on the Variable form. Each variable has an Order field that determines its position relative to other variables on the catalog item form. The Sequence field (B) and Default Value (A) serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Reports can be created from which different places in the platform? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Reports can be created from: list column headings (A) by right-clicking a column header and selecting reporting options, and the View/Run module (D) under Reports which provides report management. The Metrics module and Statistics module are not primary locations for creating reports.

questions.stem: Knowledge Base Search results can be sorted by which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Knowledge Base search results can be sorted by: Most recent update (A), Relevancy (C), and Number of views (E). These are the three standard sort options for KB search results. Popularity (B) and Manager assignment (D) are not available sort criteria for knowledge base searches.

questions.stem: What is the path an Administrator could take to view the fulfillment stage task list for an order placed by a user?
questions.explanation: The path to view fulfillment stage tasks is REQ (Request) > RITM (Requested Item) > TASK (Catalog Task). A Request (REQ) contains Requested Items (RITM), and each RITM can have Catalog Tasks (SCTASK) as fulfillment activities. This is the standard Service Catalog fulfillment hierarchy.

questions.stem: Which term refers to application menus and modules which you may want to access quickly and often?
questions.explanation: Favorites in ServiceNow allow users to bookmark application menus and modules for quick, frequent access. The star icon marks items as favorites, and they appear in the Favorites section of the Application Navigator. Breadcrumbs show navigation path, Tags categorize records, and Bookmarks are not a ServiceNow term.

questions.stem: What is generated from the Service Catalog once a user places an order for an item or service?
questions.explanation: When a user places an order from the Service Catalog, a Request (REQ) record is generated. The Request is the parent record that contains one or more Requested Items (RITM). It is not a Change Request, Order Guide, or SLA - those serve entirely different purposes in the platform.

questions.stem: From the User menu, which actions can a user select? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: From the User menu (profile icon in the banner), users can: Log Out (B), Elevate Roles (C) to security_admin, and Impersonate Users (D). Send Notifications, Order from Service Catalog, and Approve Records are not User menu actions - they are accessed through other parts of the platform.

questions.stem: Buttons, form links, and context menu items are all examples of what type of functionality?
questions.explanation: Buttons, form links, and context menu items are all examples of UI Actions. UI Actions add interactive elements to forms and lists that execute server-side or client-side code when clicked. Business Rules run automatically on database operations, Client Scripts run on form events, and UI Policies control field behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of Service Catalog Items in relation to the Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: Service Catalog Items are the building blocks of the Service Catalog. They are the fundamental units that make up the catalog - each representing a service or product that users can request. They don't run behind scenes (A), aren't optional (C), and 'provide options' (D) is too vague to describe their role.

questions.stem: Table Access Control rules are processed in the following order:

options.text: any table name (wildcard), parent table name, table name
table name, parent table name, any table name (wildcard)
parent table name, table name, any table name (wildcard)
any table name (wildcard), table name, parent table name

questions.explanation: Table Access Control rules are evaluated from most specific to most general: first the specific table name (e.g., incident), then the parent table name (e.g., task), then any table name (wildcard *). This ensures that more specific rules take precedence over general ones.

questions.stem: What is the platform name for the User table?
questions.explanation: The platform name for the User table is sys_user. The 'sys_' prefix indicates it is a system table. Tables prefixed with 'u_' are custom global tables, and 'x_' are scoped application tables. There are no tables named sys_users (plural), u_users, or x_users.

questions.stem: A REQ number in the Service Catalog represents`¦

options.text: the individual item in the order.

questions.explanation: A REQ number represents the order number in the Service Catalog. It is the parent record created when a user submits an order. The individual items in the order are represented by RITM (Requested Item) numbers, and fulfillment tasks are represented by SCTASK numbers.

questions.stem: Which would NOT appear in the History section of the Application Navigator?
questions.explanation: UI Pages would NOT appear in the History section of the Application Navigator. The History section tracks recently visited Records (A), Lists (C), and Forms (D). UI Pages are rendered in the content frame but are not tracked in the navigator history as navigable items.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is a recommendation from ServiceNow about Update Sets?

options.text: Avoid using the Default Update set as an Update Set for moving customizations from instance to instance
Before moving customizations from instance to instance with Update Sets, ensure that both instances are different versions
Use the Baseline Update Set to store the contents of items after they are changed the first time
Once an Update Set is closed as ג€Completeג€, change it back to ג€In Progressג€ until it is applied to another instance

questions.explanation: ServiceNow recommends avoiding the Default Update Set for moving customizations between instances. The Default Update Set captures changes when no other update set is selected, making it difficult to track related changes. Best practice is to create named update sets for specific projects or features.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to initiate a flow?
questions.explanation: A Trigger is used to initiate a flow in Flow Designer. Triggers define the conditions that cause a flow to start executing, such as a record being created/updated, a schedule, or an application event. Core Actions and Spokes are flow components but don't initiate flows. Events can trigger flows but the mechanism is the Trigger.

questions.stem: For Administrators creating new Service Catalog items, what is a characteristic they should know about Service Catalog variables?

options.text: Service Catalog variables can only be used in Record Producers
Service Catalog variables can only be used in Order Guides
Service Catalog variables cannot affect the order price
Service Catalog variables are global by default

questions.explanation: Service Catalog variables are global by default, meaning they can be used across different catalog items and order guides. They are not limited to Record Producers (A) or Order Guides (B) only. Variables CAN affect order price (C) through pricing scripts. The global default nature is the key characteristic admins should know.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is true about Column Context Menus?

options.text: It displays actions such as creating quick reports, configuring the list, and exporting data
It displays actions related to filtering options, assigning tags, and search
It displays actions related to viewing and filtering the entire list
It displays actions such as view form, view related task, and add relationship

questions.explanation: Column Context Menus display actions such as creating quick reports, configuring the list, and exporting data. When you right-click a column header, you get options like Sort, Group By, Bar Chart, Pie Chart, Configure, and Export. Options B and C describe different context menus (list header, breadcrumb).

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow products can be used to discover and populate the CMDB? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Discovery (A) automatically scans the network to find and populate CIs in the CMDB, and IntegrationHub ETL (B) imports CI data from external sources using extract-transform-load processes. Finder, CMDB Plug-in, and CMDB Integration Dashboard are not products designed specifically for discovering and populating the CMDB.

questions.stem: When using the Load Data and Transform Map process, what is the Mapping Assist used for?

options.text: Mapping fields using the Import Log
Mapping fields using a Field Map

questions.explanation: Mapping Assist is used for mapping fields using a Field Map during the Load Data and Transform Map process. It provides a visual interface to map source columns to target table fields by suggesting field matchings. It does not use Import Log (A), Transform History (B), or SLAs (C) for mapping.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements describes the contents of the Configuration Management Database (CMDB)?

options.text: The CMDB contains data about tangible and intangible business assets
The CMDB contains the Business Rules that direct the intangible, configurable assets used by a company
The CMDB archives all Service Management PaaS equipment metadata and usage statistics
The CMDB contains ITIL process data pertaining to configuration items

questions.explanation: The CMDB contains data about tangible and intangible business assets - both physical (servers, switches) and logical (applications, services) configuration items. It is not limited to Business Rules (B), PaaS metadata (C), or ITIL process data (D). The CMDB stores the actual CI records and their relationships.

questions.stem: In what order should filter elements be specified?
questions.explanation: Filter elements should be specified in this order: Field (which column to filter on), Operator (how to compare, e.g., is, contains, starts with), then Value (the comparison value). This Field > Operator > Value pattern is the standard filter condition structure throughout ServiceNow.

questions.stem: Which statement is true about business rules?

options.text: A business rule must run before a database action occurs
A business rule can be a piece of Javascript
A business rule must not run before a database action occurs
A business rule monitors fields on a form

questions.explanation: A Business Rule can be a piece of JavaScript that runs on the server when records are displayed, inserted, updated, or deleted. Business Rules don't MUST run before database actions (A) - they can run before, after, async, or on display. They don't monitor fields on forms (D) - that's UI Policies.

questions.stem: Which of the following are a type of client scripts supported in ServiceNow? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four types of client scripts in ServiceNow are: onLoad (D) runs when form loads, onChange (F) runs when a field value changes, onSubmit (A) runs when form is submitted, and onCellEdit (C) runs when a cell is edited in a list. onUpdate (B), onEdit (E), and onSave (G) are not valid client script types.

questions.stem: Which type of tables may be extended by other tables, but do not extend another table?
questions.explanation: Base Tables may be extended by other tables but do not themselves extend another table. They sit at the root of the table hierarchy (e.g., Task is a base table). Core Tables is not a specific ServiceNow concept for this purpose. Extended Tables are the ones doing the extending, and Custom Tables may or may not extend other tables.

questions.stem: Which of the following statement describes the purpose of an Order Guide?

options.text: Order Guides restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request
Order Guide provide a list of guidelines for Administrators on how to set up item variables
Order Guide provide the ability to order multiple, related items as one request
Order Guides take the user directly to the checkout without prompting for information

questions.explanation: An Order Guide provides the ability to order multiple, related items as one request. It bundles several catalog items together into a single ordering experience, guiding the user through a multi-step process. Order Guides don't restrict items (A), aren't setup guidelines (B), and don't skip prompting (D).

questions.stem: Which tool is used to have conversations with logged-in users in real-time?
questions.explanation: Connect Chat is the tool used for real-time conversations with logged-in users in ServiceNow. It enables instant messaging directly within the platform. User Presence shows availability status but doesn't provide chat. Comments are asynchronous journal entries. Now Messenger was a later addition but Connect Chat is the classic answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following concepts are associated with the ServiceNow CMDB? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Four CMDB concepts are: Service Processes (A) which the CMDB supports, Tables and Fields (C) that store CI data, a Database (D) as the underlying storage, and the Dependency View (E) showing CI relationships. User Permissions (B) is a platform security concept, not specifically a CMDB concept.

questions.stem: What is a formatter? Select one of the following.

options.text: A formatter allows you to configure applications on your instance
A formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field in the record
A formatter allows you to populate fields automatically
A formatter is a set of conditions applied to a table to help find and work with data

questions.explanation: A formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field in the record. Examples include the Activity formatter (shows work notes/comments history) and the Process Flow formatter (shows workflow stages). Formatters display non-field content on forms, unlike regular fields that map to database columns.

questions.stem: When searching using the App Navigator search field, what can be returned? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: When searching the App Navigator filter field, results include: Names of Applications and Modules together (A), Names of Modules (B), Names of Applications (C), and Favorites (D). History Records (E) appear in the History section but not as search results. Dashboard Gauge titles (F) are not searchable from the navigator.

questions.stem: Which technique is used to get information from a series of referenced fields from different tables?
questions.explanation: Dot-Walking is the technique used to traverse referenced fields across different tables. By using dot notation (e.g., caller_id.department.name), you can access fields from related records through reference fields. Table-Walking, Sys_ID Pulling, and Record-Hopping are not ServiceNow terminology.

questions.stem: What is a schema map?

options.text: A schema map enables administrators to define records from specific tables as trouble sources for Configuration Items
A schema map graphically organizes the visual task boards for the CMDB
A schema map graphically displays the Configuration Items that support a business service
A schema map displays the details of tables and their relationships in a visual manner, allowing administrators to view and easily access different parts of the database schema

questions.explanation: A schema map displays the details of tables and their relationships in a visual manner, allowing administrators to view and easily access different parts of the database schema. It shows table structures, columns, and how tables are connected through relationships and extensions. It is not about CI dependencies (C) or task boards (B).

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best describes the purpose of an Update Set?

options.text: An Update Set allows administrators to group a series of changes into a named set and then move this set as a unit to other systems
By default, an Update Set includes customizations, Business Rules, and homepages
An Update Set is a group of customizations that is moved from Production to Development
By default, the changes included in an Update Set are visible only in the instance to which they are applied

questions.explanation: An Update Set allows administrators to group a series of changes into a named set and then move this set as a unit to other systems. This is the primary mechanism for migrating customizations between instances (dev to test to prod). Update Sets don't include homepages by default (B), don't move from prod to dev (C).

questions.stem: Which of the following can be customized through the Basic Configuration UI 16 module? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Through Basic Configuration UI16, you can customize: Banner Image (A) to display your company logo, Browser Tab Title (C) to show custom text in the browser tab, and System Date Format (D) to change how dates are displayed. Record Number Format (B) and Form Header Size (E) are configured elsewhere.

questions.stem: What is the function of user impersonation?
questions.explanation: User impersonation is primarily for testing and visibility. It allows administrators to log in as another user to see exactly what that user sees - their menus, forms, modules, and data access. This is invaluable for troubleshooting access issues and testing configurations for different roles.

questions.stem: What information does the System Dictionary contain?

options.text: The human-readable labels and language settings
The definition for each table and column
The information on how tables relate to each other
The language dictionary used for spell checking

questions.explanation: The System Dictionary contains the definition for each table and column in the platform. It stores metadata about every table (name, label, extends) and every field (type, max length, default value, etc.). It is not about labels/languages (A), table relationships (C), or spell checking (D).

questions.stem: When working on a form, what is the difference between Insert and Update operations?

options.text: Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes, both remain on the form
Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes, both exit the form
Insert saves changes and exits the form, Update saves changes and remains on the form
Insert saves changes and remains on the form, Update saves changes and exits the form

questions.explanation: Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes to the current record - both operations exit the form and return to the previous view (typically a list). If you want to save and remain on the form, you use the Save button instead. Insert and Stay / Update and Stay are the actions that keep you on the form.

questions.stem: How is the Event Log different from the Event Registry?

options.text: Event Log contains generated Events, the Event Registry is a table of Event definitions
Event Log is formatted in the Log style, the Event Registry displays different fields
Event Log lists Events that were triggered by integrations, the Event Registry lists the Events that were triggered during the day (24-hour period)
Event Log is the same as the Event Registry

questions.explanation: The Event Log contains generated Events (actual event instances that have fired), while the Event Registry is a table of Event definitions (templates that define what events exist and how they should be processed). The Registry defines them; the Log records when they actually occur.

questions.stem: What is a Dictionary Override?

options.text: A Dictionary Override is an incoming customer update in an Update Set which applies to the same objects as a newer local customer update
A Dictionary Override is the addition, modification, or removal of anything that could have an effect on IT services
A Dictionary Override is a task within a flow that requests an action before the flow can continue
A Dictionary Override sets field properties in extended tables

questions.explanation: A Dictionary Override sets field properties in extended tables. When a child table needs different field behavior than its parent (e.g., making a field mandatory in Incident but not in Task), a Dictionary Override achieves this without changing the parent table's field definition. It is not about update conflicts (A), change management (B), or flow actions (C).

questions.stem: Which group of permissions is used to control Application and Module access?
questions.explanation: Roles are the group of permissions used to control Application and Module access. Roles determine which applications and modules appear in a user's navigator and what features they can access. ACL rules (A) protect data at table/field level. UI Policies (B) control form behavior. Assignment Rules (D) route tasks.

questions.stem: What is a Record Producer?

options.text: A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that is used for Requests, not Services
A Record Producer creates user records
A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that provides easy ordering by bundling requests
A Record Producer is a type of a Catalog Item that allows users to create task-based records from the Service Catalog

questions.explanation: A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that allows users to create task-based records from the Service Catalog. For example, a 'Create Incident' record producer lets users submit information that creates an Incident record. It doesn't just create user records (B) or bundle requests (C) - that's an Order Guide.

questions.stem: Create Incident, Password Reset, and Report outage: what do these services in the Service Catalog have in common?

options.text: They direct the user to a record producer
They direct the user to a catalog property
They direct the user to a catalog UI policy
They direct the user to a catalog client script

questions.explanation: Create Incident, Password Reset, and Report Outage are all services that direct the user to a Record Producer. Record Producers are catalog items that generate task-based records (like incidents) from the Service Catalog. They present a form to the user and create the appropriate record upon submission.

questions.stem: What is the Import Set Table?

options.text: A table where data will be placed, post-transformation
A staging area for imported records
A repository for Update Set information

questions.explanation: The Import Set Table is a staging area for imported records. When data is imported into ServiceNow, it first lands in the import set table before being transformed and written to the target table. This two-step process allows data to be reviewed and mapped before it affects production tables.

questions.stem: What is a characteristic of importing data into ServiceNow?

options.text: An existing Transform Map can be used one time on the same import set
Coalesce fields are used only after running Transform
Any user can manage and set up import sets
An existing Transform Map can be used multiple times on the same import set

questions.explanation: An existing Transform Map can be used multiple times on the same import set. This is useful when you need to re-run a transform or use the same mapping logic for subsequent data loads. Transform Maps are reusable definitions that map source columns to target fields and can be applied repeatedly.

questions.stem: What module in the Service Catalog application does an Administrator access to begin creating a new item?
questions.explanation: To create a new Service Catalog item, an administrator uses the Maintain Items module in the Service Catalog application. This module provides the interface for creating and configuring catalog items, including setting variables, workflows, and access controls.

questions.stem: Which of the following allows a user to edit field values in a list without opening the form?
questions.explanation: The List Editor allows users to edit field values directly in a list view without opening the form. By double-clicking a cell in the list, users can modify values inline. Data Editor (A) and Edit Menu (B) are not ServiceNow features. Form Designer (D) is for designing form layouts, not editing list data.

questions.stem: Which three Variable Types can be added to a Service Catalog Item?

options.text: Number List, Single Line Text, and Reference
Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox

questions.explanation: Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox are three valid variable types for Service Catalog Items. Multiple Choice provides radio buttons, Select Box provides a dropdown, and Checkbox provides a yes/no toggle. Number List (B) and Ordered (A) are not standard catalog variable types in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: How are Workflows moved between instances?

options.text: Workflows are moved using Update Sets
Workflows are moved using Transform Maps
Workflows are moved using Application Sets
Workflows cannot be moved between instances

questions.explanation: Workflows are moved between instances using Update Sets. When a workflow is modified, the changes are captured in the current Update Set, which can then be retrieved and applied to another instance. Transform Maps (B) are for data imports, Application Sets (C) is not a standard term, and workflows CAN be moved (D).

questions.stem: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains links to which of the following components?

options.text: Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
Order Guides, Item Variables, and flows
Order Guides, Catalog Items, and flows
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables

questions.explanation: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains links to Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items. These three are the core components displayed on the catalog landing page. Item Variables and flows are internal mechanisms, not top-level homepage components visible to users.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true when a new table is created by extending another table?

options.text: The new table archives the parent table and assumed its roles in the database
The new table inherits all of the Business Rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table, but none of the existing fields
The new table inherits all of the fields of the parent table and can also contain new fields unique to itself
The new table inherits all of the fields, but does not inherit Access Control rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table

questions.explanation: When a new table is created by extending another table, the new table inherits ALL fields of the parent table and can also contain new fields unique to itself. It also inherits Business Rules, Client Scripts, UI Policies, and ACLs from the parent. The new table does NOT archive or replace the parent.

questions.stem: Where can Admins check which release is running on an ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: Administrators can check which release is running on a ServiceNow instance using the Stats module (System Diagnostics > Stats). This page displays system information including the build name, build date, and release version. Memory Stats shows memory usage, not version info.

questions.stem: A knowledge article must be which of the following states to display to a user?
questions.explanation: A knowledge article must be in the Published state to be displayed to users. Articles go through a lifecycle: Draft > Review (optional) > Published > Retired. Only Published articles are visible in knowledge base searches and portals. Drafted, Retired, and Reviewed articles are not visible to end users.

questions.stem: What is the name of the conversational bot platform that provides assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common tasks?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is the conversational bot platform in ServiceNow that provides assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common tasks through a messaging interface. Answer Agent is not a product. Live Feed is a social collaboration tool. Connect Chat is for person-to-person messaging.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a Related List?

options.text: To dot-walk to a core table

questions.explanation: A Related List presents related records on a form. It displays records from another table that have a relationship to the current record (e.g., Incidents related list on a User form shows all incidents where that user is the caller). It doesn't create relationships (A), dot-walk (B), or present fields (C).

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements describes the purpose of a Service Catalog flow?

options.text: A Service Catalog flow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and approvals
Although a Service Catalog flow cannot send notifications, the flow drives complex fulfillment processes
A Service Catalog flow is used to drive complex fulfillment processes and sends notifications to defined users or groups
A Service Catalog flow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and notifications

questions.explanation: A Service Catalog flow is used to drive complex fulfillment processes AND sends notifications to defined users or groups. Flows handle the entire lifecycle of a catalog request including approvals, tasks, and notifications. Option B incorrectly says flows cannot send notifications, and A/D describe wrong components.

questions.stem: Which term best describes something that is created, has worked performed upon it, and is eventually moved to a state of closed?
questions.explanation: A Task best describes something that is created, has work performed upon it, and is eventually moved to a state of closed. The Task table is the foundational table in ServiceNow for work management, with lifecycle states from New through to Closed. Reports, flows, and events don't follow this work lifecycle.

questions.stem: Which are valid Service Now User Authentication Methods? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid ServiceNow user authentication methods are: Local database (B) where credentials are stored on the instance, LDAP (C) for directory-based authentication, and SSO/Single Sign-On (D) for federated identity. XML feed (A) and FTP authentication (E) are not authentication methods in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: Access Control rules may be defined with which of the following permission requirements? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Access Control rules can be defined with three types of permission requirements: Roles (A) specifying which roles are needed, Conditional Expressions (B) using field-based conditions, and Scripts (D) that programmatically evaluate access using the 'answer' variable. Assignment Rules (C), User Criteria (E), and Groups (F) are not ACL permission types.

questions.stem: Which section of the ServiceNow UI allows you to perform a global search?
questions.explanation: The Banner frame (header area at the top of the UI) contains the global search functionality. The global text search field in the banner allows searching across multiple tables simultaneously. The Application Navigator (A) has a filter for menus/modules but not global search. Content frame (D) displays records.

questions.stem: How do you make a list filter available to everyone?

options.text: Make active, assign a name, and save
Assign a group, set visibility, and save
Assign a name, set visibility, and save
Make active, set visibility, and save

questions.explanation: To make a list filter available to everyone: assign a name to the filter, set visibility to 'Everyone' (or specific groups), and save. The visibility setting determines who can see the saved filter. Without a name, the filter cannot be saved. Without setting visibility, it remains personal.

questions.stem: What would NOT appear in the Application Navigator if `service` is typed into the filter field?
questions.explanation: Typing 'service' in the Application Navigator filter would NOT show 'Incident > Assigned to me' because this module name doesn't contain the word 'service.' It would show Configuration > Business Services (A), Self-Service > Knowledge (B), and Service Portal > Widgets (C) since they all contain 'service' in their path.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to categorize, flag, and locate records?
questions.explanation: Tags are used to categorize, flag, and locate records in ServiceNow. Users can apply custom labels (tags) to records for easy identification and filtering. Tags can be personal or shared with others. Search (A) finds records, Favorites (B) bookmark navigation items, and Bookmarks (D) is not a ServiceNow concept.

questions.stem: Which tool should be used to populate commonly used fields in a form?
questions.explanation: Templates should be used to populate commonly used fields in a form. A template stores predefined values for multiple fields that can be applied when creating new records, saving time for repetitive data entry. Reference Qualifiers filter reference fields, Formatters display non-field info, and Assignment Rules route tasks.

questions.stem: How is a group defined in ServiceNow?

options.text: A group is one record stored in the Group Type [sys_user_group_type] table
A group is one record stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table
A group defines a set of users that share the same location
A group defines a set of users that share the same job title

questions.explanation: A group in ServiceNow is one record stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table. Each group record contains properties like name, manager, type, and email. Groups are not defined by shared location (C) or job title (D) - those are just attributes. The table name is sys_user_group, not sys_user_group_type (A).

questions.stem: What is a role in ServiceNow?

options.text: A role is one record in the Role [user_sys_role] table
A role is a set of modules for a particular application
A role is one record in the Role [sys_user_role] table
A role is a persona used in Live Feed Chat

questions.explanation: A role in ServiceNow is one record in the Role [sys_user_role] table. Each role record defines a set of permissions that can be assigned to users or groups. The correct table name is sys_user_role, not user_sys_role (A). A role is not a set of modules (B) or a Live Feed persona (D).

questions.stem: What is a Notification?

options.text: A new Knowledge article created by a Business Rule
A tool for alerting users that events that concern them have occurred
A message through Connect related to a Change Request

questions.explanation: A Notification is a tool for alerting users that events that concern them have occurred. Notifications can be sent via email, SMS, or meeting invitations when specific conditions are met (e.g., incident assigned, approval requested). It is not a KB article (A), Connect message (C), or email attachment (D).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a type of Visual Task Board?
questions.explanation: Feature is NOT a type of Visual Task Board in ServiceNow. The three valid types are: Flexible (A) for customizable boards, Freeform (B) for unstructured boards, and Guided boards (D) with predefined lanes. Feature boards do not exist as a Visual Task Board type.

questions.stem: What is (are) best practice(s) regarding users/groups/roles? (Choose two.)

options.text: You should never assign roles to groups.
You should assign roles to users.
You should add users to groups.
You should assign roles to groups.

questions.explanation: Best practices for users/groups/roles: you should add users to groups (C) to organize team members, and assign roles to groups (D) so all group members inherit the permissions. You should NOT assign roles directly to individual users (B) as it becomes difficult to manage at scale. Never assigning roles to groups (A) is wrong.

questions.stem: What are two ways to generate an Event? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Two ways to generate an Event in ServiceNow are: Business Rules (A) using gs.eventQueue() in server-side scripts, and Workflows (B) using the Create Event activity. Log entries (C) and Knowledge article publication (D) do not generate events in the Event Registry/Event Log directly.

questions.stem:
Which core table in the ServiceNow platform provides a series of standard fields used on each of the tables that extend it, such as the Incident [incident] and
Problem [problem] tables?
questions.explanation: The Task [task] table is the core table that provides standard fields (number, state, assignment group, priority, etc.) used by all extending tables like Incident, Problem, and Change Request. The Task table is the foundational work-management table in the ServiceNow platform.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes how data is organized in a table?

options.text: A column is a field in the database and a record is one user
A column is one field and a record is one row
A column is one field and a record is one column
A column contains data from one user and a record is one set of fields

questions.explanation: In a ServiceNow table, a column represents one field (e.g., 'State' or 'Priority') and a record represents one row of data (e.g., one specific incident). Each row contains data across all the columns/fields defined for that table. This is standard relational database terminology.

questions.stem: What is a sys_id?

options.text: Unique 32-character identifier that is assigned to every record
Unique 64-character identifier that is assigned to every record

questions.explanation: A sys_id is a unique 32-character identifier (GUID) automatically assigned to every record in every table in ServiceNow. It serves as the primary key for all records. It is 32 characters (not 64 as in D), and is not a type of Business Rule (B or C).

questions.stem: When creating a global custom table named `abc`, what is the table name that is automatically assigned by the platform?
questions.explanation: When creating a global custom table named 'abc', the platform automatically prepends 'u_' to create 'u_abc'. The 'u_' prefix denotes user-created (custom) tables in the global scope. The 'x_' prefix is for scoped application tables, 'snc_' for ServiceNow created tables, and 'sys_' for system tables.

questions.stem: Access Control rules may provide access security for which of the following database objects?

options.text: For a specific role, group, or user
For a specific row, column, or table
For a specific CMDB Configuration item

questions.explanation: Access Control rules provide access security for specific database objects: rows (record-level), columns (field-level), or tables (table-level). ACLs protect these three levels of data objects. They are not specifically for roles/groups/users (A) - those are the permissions on the ACL. They're not for specific groups (C) or CMDB CIs (D).

questions.stem: What is the primary application used to load data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: System Import Sets is the primary application used to load data into ServiceNow from external sources. It provides the complete import pipeline: loading data into staging tables, creating transform maps, and running transforms to write to target tables. Service Level Management, Configuration, and System Update Sets serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Which of the following steps can be used to import new data into ServiceNow from a spreadsheet?

options.text: Load Data, Create Transform Map, Run Transform
Define Data Source, Select Transform Map, Run Transform
Select Import Set, Select Transform Map, Run Transform

questions.explanation: The steps to import data from a spreadsheet are: Load Data (upload the file to a staging table), Create Transform Map (define field mappings from staging to target), and Run Transform (execute the mapping to write data to the target table). This three-step process is the standard import workflow.

questions.stem: Which tool is used for creating dependencies between configuration items in the CMDB?
questions.explanation: The CI Relationship Editor is used for creating dependencies (relationships) between configuration items in the CMDB. It provides a visual interface to add, modify, or remove relationships such as 'Depends on', 'Runs on', or 'Used by' between CIs. CMDB Builder, CI Service Manager, and CI Class Manager serve different purposes.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a UI Policy and Data Policy?

options.text: Data Policies run when data is entered through the form, by an Import Set, or by web services, while UI Policies are set only by web services
Data Policies can be converted into UI Policies, but UI Policies cannot be converted into Data Policies
Data Policies run regardless of how data is entered into ServiceNow, while UI Policies are used for form interactions
Data Policies run only after UI Policies run successfully

questions.explanation: Data Policies run regardless of how data is entered into ServiceNow (UI, Import Sets, web services, or scripts), enforcing rules at the server/database level. UI Policies only apply to form interactions in the browser. This is the fundamental difference: Data Policies are server-enforced, UI Policies are client-enforced.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is an accurate list of changes that are captured in an Update Set?

options.text: Changes made to: tables, forms, schedules, and client scripts
Changes made to: tables, forms, Business Rules, and data records
Changes made to: tables, forms, groups, and configuration items (CIs)
Changes made to: table, forms, views, and fields

questions.explanation: An Update Set captures changes made to tables, forms, views, and fields. These are configuration/customization changes. Update Sets do NOT capture data records (B), group membership (C), or configuration items. They track metadata about the platform structure, not the data itself.

questions.stem: What are the steps to retrieve an Update Set?

options.text: Verify Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Apply
Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Apply
Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Commit
Verify Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Commit

questions.explanation: The steps to retrieve an Update Set are: Verify Update Set is Complete (ensure it's marked complete on source), Retrieve (pull it from the remote instance), Preview (check for conflicts or issues), and Commit (apply the changes). 'Apply' is not the final step - 'Commit' is the correct ServiceNow terminology.

questions.stem: IntegrationHub enables execution of third-party APIs as a part of a flow. These integrations are referred to as
questions.explanation: IntegrationHub's third-party API integrations are referred to as Spokes. A spoke is a scoped application containing Flow Designer actions, subflows, and connection info for integrating with a specific third-party service (e.g., Slack spoke, Jira spoke). Actions (A) are individual steps within spokes.

questions.stem: Which of the following protects applications by identifying and restricting access to available files and data?
questions.explanation: Application Scope protects applications by identifying and restricting access to available files and data. Scoped applications run in their own namespace, preventing other applications from directly accessing their tables, scripts, and records without explicit cross-scope access granted. ACL rules (C) protect data, not application boundaries.

questions.stem: Which one statement correctly describes Access Control rule evaluation?

options.text: Table access rules are evaluated from the general to the specific
If more than one rule applies to a record, the older rule is evaluated first
If a row level rule and a field level rule exist, both rules must be true before an operation is allowed
The role with the most permissions evaluates the rules first.

questions.explanation: If both a row-level rule and a field-level rule exist for a record, both rules must evaluate to true before the operation is allowed. ACL evaluation is cumulative - the system checks table-level, then row-level, then field-level rules, and all applicable rules must pass. This ensures layered security.

questions.stem:
ServiceNow contains a resource which provides the following:
✑ A standard and shared set of service related definitions across ServiceNow products and platform that will enable and support true service level reporting.
✑ A CMDB framework across our products and platform that will enable and support multiple configuration strategies.
What resource do these statements describe?
questions.explanation: The Common Services Data Model (CSDM) provides a standard, shared set of service-related definitions and a CMDB framework across ServiceNow products. CSDM defines how to organize CIs, services, and applications in the CMDB to support reporting and management. ITSM is a practice framework, CMDB is the database, and ITIL is a methodology.

questions.stem: An IT manager is responsible for the Network and Hardware assignment groups, each group contains 5 team members. These team members are working on many tasks, but the manager cannot see any tasks on the Service Desk > My Groups Work list. What could explain this?

options.text: The Service Desk > My Groups Work list shows active work tasks that are not yet assigned.
The manager does not have the itil role.
The manager is not a member of the Service Desk group.
The manager is not a member of the Network and Hardware groups.
The Assignment Group manager field is empty.

questions.explanation: The manager cannot see tasks on My Groups Work because they are not a member of the Network and Hardware groups. The 'My Groups Work' list shows tasks assigned to groups the logged-in user belongs to. Even though the manager manages these groups (via the manager field), they must be an actual member to see group work in this list.

questions.stem: What do you need to do before you can use an Application-based trigger in your flow?

options.text: Activate application spoke, and plug-ins as needed
Assign Application trigger role [sn_app_trigger_write] to SME

questions.explanation: Before using an application-based trigger in a flow, you must activate the application spoke and any required plugins. Application-based triggers depend on the underlying application's spoke being active and properly configured. Simply activating trigger security rules or assigning roles is not sufficient.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow platform includes which types of interfaces? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow platform includes three types of interfaces: Now Mobile Apps (A) for mobile device access, Service Portals (D) for self-service web interfaces, and Now Platform User Interfaces (E) for the agent/admin desktop experience. Agent Control Center, Back Office Dashboard, and Field Service Taskboard are not platform interface types.

questions.stem: Which of the following are not included in an Update Set, by default? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Items NOT included in an Update Set by default: Data/records (B), Schedules (E), Scheduled Jobs (F), and Report Definitions (I - in some versions). Homepages (A) are also excluded but are not one of the four required answers here. Business Rules (D), Database changes (F), Client Scripts (J), and Views (K) ARE captured.

questions.stem:
You are showing your customer a new form that you have created for their new application. They would like to add a field to the form. Where could you do that?
(Choose two.)

options.text: Click on context menu, select Admin view
Right click on form header, select Configure > Form Layout
Click on context menu, select Configure > Form Designer

questions.explanation: Two ways to add fields to a form: right-click on the form header and select Configure > Form Layout (D) to use the list collector, or use the context menu and select Configure > Form Designer (E) for a drag-and-drop interface. These are the two standard methods for modifying form layout.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow resource is a framework that ensures the data your ServiceNow application requires maps correctly to the appropriate CMDB tables?
questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) is the framework that ensures data required by ServiceNow applications maps correctly to appropriate CMDB tables. CSDM provides a standardized data model and table structure for organizing services, applications, and infrastructure in the CMDB.

questions.stem: What do you activate when you want to add applications or functionality within your development instance?
questions.explanation: To add applications or functionality to a development instance, you activate a Plugin. Plugins are pre-built packages that add features, tables, and functionality to the instance. They are activated through System Definition > Plugins. App Packages, Update Packs, Patches, and App Installers are not the correct ServiceNow terminology.

questions.stem: What field contains a record's 32-character, unique identifier?
questions.explanation: The sys_id field contains a record's 32-character unique identifier. Every record in every ServiceNow table has a sys_id that serves as its primary key. The field is automatically generated and is a 32-character GUID. No other field names listed (sn_rec_id, rec_id, u_id, etc.) are standard ServiceNow identifiers.

questions.stem: Your company is giving all first line workers a special T-shirt as a recognition for their hard work. Management team wants a way for employees to order the T- shirt, with the ability to specify the preferred size and color. How would you ensure that only first line workers (non-managers) can submit the order?

options.text: Create Record Producer and use the Available For list to specify First Line [sn_first_line] role
Create Catalog Item and use the Not Available list to specify the Manager Group
Create Catalog Item and use the Available For list to specify ITIL [itil] role
Create Order Guide and use the User Criteria list to specify First Line [sn_first_line] role

questions.explanation: Create a Catalog Item and use the Not Available list to specify the Manager Group. By adding the Manager Group to the 'Not available for' User Criteria, managers are excluded from seeing/ordering the item while all other users (including first line workers) can access it. This is simpler than creating specific roles.

questions.stem: What is used frequently to move customizations from one instance to another?
questions.explanation: Update Sets are used frequently to move customizations from one instance to another (e.g., dev to test to production). They capture configuration changes made in one instance and allow them to be transferred and applied to other instances. Code Sets, Update Packs, and other options are not ServiceNow terminology.

questions.stem: What icon do you use to change the label on a Favorite?
questions.explanation: The Pencil icon is used to change the label (name) on a Favorite. When you hover over a favorite in the Application Navigator, clicking the pencil icon lets you edit its display name. The Star icon creates/removes favorites. The Clock relates to history. Hamburger and Three dots are for other menus.

questions.stem: What needs to be specified, when creating a Business Rule? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: When creating a Business Rule, you must specify: Table (B) it applies to, Script to run (E) defining the logic, Timing/When (H) it executes (before/after/async/display), and Condition to evaluate (I) determining when it triggers. UI Actions, Fields to update, who can run, Application scope, and Update set are not required BR specifications.

questions.stem: What feature can track the amount of time that a task has been open, to ensure that tasks are completed within an allotted time?
questions.explanation: Service Level Agreements (SLAs) track the amount of time a task has been open to ensure tasks are completed within an allotted time frame. SLAs define target response and resolution times and can trigger escalations when breached. Task Escalation Clock, Inactivity Monitor, and Response Time Clock are not the primary feature for this.

questions.stem: What is a quick way to create a report from a list view?

options.text: Click on filter breadcrumb, drag and drop on the Report > Create New module
Click Funnel, define filter conditions, click Create Report
Click Context Menu, select Create Report
Apply filter, right click on column header, select Bar Chart
Apply filter, right click on column header, select Create Report

questions.explanation: A quick way to create a report from a list view is to apply a filter, right-click on a column header, and select Bar Chart (or Pie Chart). This instantly generates a report visualization based on the filtered list data grouped by that column. This is faster than navigating to the Reports module.

questions.stem: What import utility do you use when the field names on the import set match the name of the fields on the Target table?
questions.explanation: Automatic Mapping is used when the field names on the import set match the names of the fields on the target table. It automatically maps columns by matching column names, saving time when source and target field names align. Schema Mapping (A), Mapping Assist (C), and Mapping Dashboard (D) serve different purposes.

questions.stem: As an IT employee what interface would you use, if you wanted to browse internal IT documentation, like troubleshooting scripts and FAQs?
questions.explanation: As an IT employee, you would use the Knowledge application to browse internal IT documentation like troubleshooting scripts and FAQs. ServiceNow Knowledge Management provides a centralized repository for creating, categorizing, and searching organizational knowledge articles.

questions.stem: A new Service Desk employee in Latin America complains that the create dates and times are incorrect on their Incident list. What would you suggest to fix this issue?

options.text: Have them use the gear icon to set the employee's time zone.
Recommend they use Chrome, instead of Explorer.
Use the system properties to correct the instance's time zone.
Have them correct the time zone on their computer.

questions.explanation: The Service Desk employee should use the gear icon (system settings) to set their personal time zone. Each user can configure their own time zone preference through the system settings gear icon in the banner. This adjusts date/time displays for that user without affecting other users or the instance time zone.

questions.stem: What are three security modules often used by the System Administrator? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Three security modules used by System Administrators: System Properties > Security (A) for security-related system properties, System Security > Access Control/ACL (E) for managing access control rules, and System Security > High Security Settings (G) for elevated security configuration. These are the primary admin security modules.

questions.stem: When testing a catalog item, having a manager approval flows, which of these best practices would you follow? (Choose three.)

options.text: Make sure the latest flows are activated.
Use the instance Incognito setting to quickly toggle between requester and approver.
Impersonate the requester to ensure the form works.
Make sure the requester's user record has a manager specified.
Create and select your Testing Update Set, before starting the test cases.
Use your Admin account, so you can approve the items quickly.

questions.explanation: Best practices for testing catalog items with approval flows: make sure the latest flows are activated (A) so the approval flow runs correctly, impersonate the requester (C) to test the form as an end user, and ensure the requester's user record has a manager specified (D) for the approval to route properly.

questions.stem: What is a no-code approach to control the mandatory or read-only state of a form field?
questions.explanation: A UI Policy is the no-code approach to control the mandatory, read-only, or visible state of a form field. UI Policies are configured through a point-and-click interface without writing any scripts. UI Actions (A) add buttons/links, Client Scripts (B) and UI Scripts (C) require coding, and UI Rule (D) is not a standard feature.

questions.stem: When moving multiple update sets at one time, what might you do to facilitate the move?
questions.explanation: When moving multiple update sets at one time, you can Merge them to combine several update sets into a single batch update set. This consolidates related changes and simplifies the transfer process. You would merge the updates sets first, then retrieve and apply the merged set on the target instance.

questions.stem: What is specified in an Access Control rule?

options.text: Table Schema, CRUD, and User Authentication
Object and Operation being secured; Permissions required to access the object

questions.explanation: An Access Control rule specifies: the Object and Operation being secured (which table/field and what CRUD operation), and the Permissions required to access that object (roles, conditions, scripts). This is the fundamental structure of an ACL. Groups/Workflows (A), Table Schema/CRUD/Auth (B), and security_admin (D) don't describe this correctly.

questions.stem: Which icon would you double click, to expand and collapse the list of all Applications and Modules?
questions.explanation: Double-clicking the Application icon (globe/compass icon) in the Application Navigator expands or collapses the full list of all Applications and Modules. The Star icon (A) accesses Favorites, the Clock (B) shows History, and the Funnel (D) opens the filter for the navigator.

questions.stem: What do you call any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver services?
questions.explanation: A Configuration Item (CI) is any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver services. CIs are stored in the CMDB and can be tangible (servers, routers) or intangible (applications, services). CSDM Items, CMDB, Service Offerings, and Assets are related but don't define this specific concept.

questions.stem: A new service catalog item is being developed, but should only be visible to managers inside the HR Department. What method would you use to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Specify the Dept_Mgr role on the catalog content block
Add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's user criteria
Add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's ACL
Only publish the item in the HR service catalog
Use a Dept_Mgr ACL on the HR service catalog

questions.explanation: To make a catalog item visible only to managers in the HR Department, add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's User Criteria. User Criteria on catalog items defines who can see and order the item based on group membership, department, role, or other attributes. This is the standard approach for catalog item visibility.

questions.stem:
A user wants to create a set of filter conditions, where they want to show records which satisfy two conditions:
✑ Incidents where the state is Closed
✑ Incidents where Assignment Group is Network
After clicking the Funnel icon, what should the user do?

options.text: Define the first condition; click AND button; define second condition; click Run
Define the first condition; click AND button; define second condition; press enter
Define the first condition; click OR button; define second condition; press enter
Define the first condition; click > icon on breadcrumb, define second condition; click Run
Define the first condition; click > icon on breadcrumb, define second condition; press enter

questions.explanation: To show records matching two conditions (State is Closed AND Assignment Group is Network): define the first condition, click the AND button to add a second condition, define the second condition, then click Run. The AND operator requires both conditions to be true simultaneously. OR (C) would match either condition.

questions.stem:
Access Control rules are applied to a specific table, like the Incident table. What is the object name for a rule that is specific to the Incident table and the Major
Incident field?
questions.explanation: The ACL object name for a rule specific to the Incident table and the Major Incident field is incident.major_incident (lowercase table.field with a dot separator). This follows the standard ACL naming convention: tablename.fieldname. The dot notation separates the table from the field in the ACL object name.

questions.stem:
Two departments (HR Onboarding and Facilities) have come to you, asking for a way for employees to request event room set up services. The requirements are the same for the form and the task routing to the Facilities' assignment group.
✑ For HR, the item will be used primarily for the Onboarding coordinators, for employee orientation sessions.
✑ For Facilities, the item will be used for anyone in the company who needs room set up services.
However, both departments have their own service catalogs. What do you do, to support these requirements?

options.text: Create one Catalog Item for HR Event Room Set Up and one for Facilities Event Room Set Up; then publish each to the appropriate Catalog.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then publish to both Catalogs.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then publish to the Parent Catalog, which is accessible to both HR and Facilities.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then use ACLs to control access.

questions.explanation: Since both departments need the same form and task routing, create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up, then publish it to both catalogs. A single catalog item can be published to multiple service catalogs, avoiding duplication. There's no need to create two separate items (A) when the requirements are identical.

questions.stem: After finishing your work on High Security Settings, what do you do to return to normal admin security levels?

options.text: Use System Administration > Normal Security module

questions.explanation: After finishing with High Security Settings, you log out and back in to return to normal admin security levels. Elevated roles (security_admin) are session-based and persist until the session ends. Logging out terminates the elevated session. There is no 'Normal role' selection or 'Normal Security' module.

questions.stem: What type of field allows you to look up values from one other table?
questions.explanation: A Reference field allows you to look up values from one other table. It creates a relationship between the current table and a referenced table, displaying a lookup icon that lets users search and select a record from the referenced table (e.g., the Caller field on Incident references sys_user).

questions.stem: Which module would you use to create a new automation of business logic such as approvals, tasks, and notifications?
questions.explanation: Process Automation > Flow Designer is the module used to create new automation of business logic including approvals, tasks, and notifications. Flow Designer provides a visual, low-code interface for building automated workflows. Flow Administration (B) manages existing flows, and Workflow Editor (C) is the legacy tool.

questions.stem: A department manager asks an analyst to build some reports. Where do you recommend the analyst start?
questions.explanation: To create reports, the analyst should start with Reports > Create New. This module provides the Report Designer interface where you configure the data source, type, grouping, and styling of a new report. The other paths either don't exist or don't lead to report creation directly.

questions.stem: What are the steps for applying an update set to an instance?
questions.explanation: The steps for applying an update set to an instance are: Retrieve (pull the update set from the remote instance), Preview (check for conflicts and issues), and Commit (apply the changes to the instance). This is the standard three-step process. Assess, Apply, Push, Pull, and Review are not the correct terms.

questions.stem: When importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow, in which step does the data get written to the receiving table?
questions.explanation: During the import process, the Run Transform step writes data to the receiving (target) table. The transform map defines how source columns map to target fields, and running the transform executes those mappings. Load Data only puts data in the staging table; Run Transform moves it to the final destination.

questions.stem: What would you do, on a list, if you wanted to show the records in groups, based on the column category? (Choose two.)

options.text: On list Context Menu, select Group By > Category
On the Filter Menu, select Group By > Category
Click Group On icon, select Category
On Navigator Filter, type tablename.group.category and press enter
On the Category column title, click Context menu > Group By Category

questions.explanation: Two ways to group records by category in a list: use the list Context Menu and select Group By > Category (A), or on the Category column title, click the column context menu and select Group By Category (E). Both achieve the same result of organizing list records into groups based on the Category field value.

questions.stem: Which collaboration tool is available from the banner, using the bubble icon?
questions.explanation: Connect Chat is the collaboration tool available from the banner using the bubble/chat icon. It allows real-time messaging with other ServiceNow users directly within the platform. Now Messenger is a newer feature. Agent Chat is for customer service. Collaborate Now and Live Feed are different tools.

questions.stem: On the knowledge base record, which tab would you use to define which users are not able to write articles to the knowledge base?
questions.explanation: The 'Cannot Contribute' tab on the knowledge base record defines which users are NOT able to write articles to that knowledge base. User Criteria on this tab explicitly excludes specified users or groups from contributing content. 'Can Contribute' (A) is the positive permission, 'Cannot Author' (B) is not a standard tab.

questions.stem: Which features allow you to update multiple records at one time? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Two features for updating multiple records at once: List Editor (A) allows inline editing of multiple records directly in the list view, and Update Selected Action (E) lets you select multiple records via checkboxes and apply bulk changes. These are the standard multi-record editing capabilities in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: Categories in the knowledge base, by default, can be created and edited by which knowledge workers? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: By default, Knowledge Contributors (B) and Knowledge Managers (D) can create and edit categories in a knowledge base. Contributors have write access to the KB including category management, and Managers have full administrative control over the knowledge base structure including categories.

questions.stem: Which collaboration tool opens a sidebar and allows you to create new conversations with other ServiceNow users?
questions.explanation: Agent Chat opens a sidebar and allows you to create new conversations with other ServiceNow users. In newer versions of ServiceNow, Agent Chat (also known as Connect Chat or messaging) provides the sidebar-based real-time messaging experience. The sidebar opens from the banner and lists active conversations.

questions.stem: What module would you use if you wanted to view a list of all of the fields on the Incident table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: To view a list of all fields on the Incident table, use Tables & Columns (A) which shows table structure with all fields, or Dictionary (B) which contains the definition of every table and column. Both modules allow you to see all fields defined for a specific table.

questions.stem: What component causes a flow to run after a record has been created or updated?
questions.explanation: A Record-based trigger causes a flow to run after a record has been created or updated. It monitors a specified table for insert or update operations and triggers the flow when conditions are met. Date-based triggers (A) use schedules, On-change (B) is not a standard trigger type, and Application-based (D) triggers require spoke activation.

questions.stem: What type of field is Boolean and appears as a check box?
questions.explanation: A True/False field type is Boolean and appears as a check box on ServiceNow forms. When checked, the value is true; when unchecked, the value is false. This is the standard representation of Boolean data on forms. Yes/No, On/Off, Binary, and 0/1 are not the ServiceNow field type names.

questions.stem: Which module is used to access the knowledge bases which are available to you?
questions.explanation: Self Service > Knowledge is the module used to access knowledge bases available to you. This is the standard navigation path for end users and IT staff to browse and search knowledge articles. Knowledge > Home (A), Knowledge > All (C), and other paths are not the primary user-facing knowledge module.

questions.stem:
A customer requests the following data quality measures be added:
✑ Incident numbers should be read only, on all lists and forms, for all users.
✑ Short Description field should be mandatory, on all records, across all applications, on Insert.
Which type of policy would you use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Data Policy is the correct choice because the requirements specify enforcement across all records and all applications (including lists, forms, imports, and web services). Data Policies run server-side regardless of how data is entered, making Incident numbers read-only and Short Description mandatory everywhere. UI Policy (D) only works on forms.

questions.stem: What type of user (persona) has clearly defined paths and workflows in the platform and have one or more roles (ie itil and approver_user)?
questions.explanation: A Process User has clearly defined paths and workflows in the platform and has one or more roles (like itil and approver_user). Process Users follow structured processes for their work - they are the standard persona type for users who interact with ITSM workflows. Request Fulfillers, ITSM Users, and Service Desk Users are too specific.

questions.stem: Which module would you use to customize your instances banner image, text and colors?
questions.explanation: System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16 is the module used to customize the instance's banner image, text, and colors. This module provides a simple interface for branding customization including logo, banner text, header colors, and theme. The other paths listed are not correct for these branding settings.

questions.stem: Which database provides a logical model of your company infrastructure by identifying, controlling, maintaining and verifying CIs that exist?
questions.explanation: The Configuration Management Database (CMDB) provides a logical model of company infrastructure by identifying, controlling, maintaining, and verifying CIs. It stores configuration items and their relationships to support IT service management. IMDB is a movie database, ITSM is a practice, CSDM is a data model, and LDAP is directory authentication.

questions.stem: Which module is used as the first step for importing data?
questions.explanation: Load Data is the first step for importing data. It uploads the source file (CSV, Excel, XML) into a staging import set table. After loading, you create a transform map and then run the transform. Coalesce, Transform, and Import are subsequent steps in the process, not the first.

questions.stem: When you need to orchestrate business processes across services with little technical user knowledge, which utility would you use?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer is the utility for orchestrating business processes across services with little technical user knowledge. It provides a visual, low-code/no-code interface for building automation. The Workflow Editor (D) is the legacy tool requiring more technical knowledge. Flow Manager, Flow Editor, and Workflow Designer are not correct names.

questions.stem: When a user reports that they are not able to see modules on the application navigator, what can you do, to see what modules are visible to them?

options.text: Look up their password, so you can login with their account

questions.explanation: To see what modules are visible to a user who reports missing modules, you should Impersonate the user. Impersonation lets you see the exact same interface the user sees, including which applications and modules are visible based on their roles and group memberships. This is the fastest and safest diagnostic approach.

questions.stem: What is a key difference between Reporting and Performance Analytics?

options.text: Performance Analytics contains snapshots of data taken over time; Reporting shows only the data as it is, at the moment the report is run.
Performance Analytics can show trends; Reports cannot.
Reports can be run on a scheduled basis; Performance Analytics cannot.
Performance Analytics data can be published to Dashboards; Reports cannot.
Performance Analytics shows KPIs; Reporting does not.

questions.explanation: The key difference is that Performance Analytics contains snapshots of data taken over time (historical tracking), while Reporting shows only the data as it exists at the moment the report is run (point-in-time). PA collects and stores scores at regular intervals enabling trend analysis. Reports are real-time snapshots without historical context.

questions.stem:
While showing a customer their incident form, they ask to change the Priority values to display their internal terminology P1, P2, P3, P4. They want it to be consistent across all Tasks. How would you do that?
Right click on Priority and select what?
questions.explanation: To change the Priority values to display custom terminology (P1, P2, P3, P4) consistently across all Tasks, right-click on Priority and select Show Choice List. This opens the choice list editor where you can modify the display labels for each priority value across the Task table and all its children.

questions.stem: Your customer would like to create a new template to notify users who are affected by network outages at their site. Which module would you use to create a new notification?
questions.explanation: System Notification > Email > Notifications is the module used to create a new notification template. This is the standard path to the Notification table where you configure who receives the notification, under what conditions, and what content it contains. The other paths are incorrect or don't exist.

questions.stem: When designing a flow, how do you reference data from a record, in that flow?

options.text: Drag the table icon onto the flow definition
Use the condition builder to specify the desired values
Specify the source table on the data pill related list
Drag the data pill onto the flow definition
Add the table reference using the slush bucket

questions.explanation: In Flow Designer, you reference data from a record by dragging a Data Pill onto the flow definition. Data Pills are visual representations of data values that can be dragged into action inputs. They allow you to pass data between flow steps without coding. Condition builders and slush buckets are used for other purposes.

questions.stem: On the Reports page, what sections allow you to see which reports are visible to different audiences? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The Reports page sections for viewing reports by audience are: Group (A) for group-shared reports, My reports (C) for personal reports, Global (F) for reports visible to everyone, and All (I) for all accessible reports combined. Department (B), Dashboards (E), Team (D), Admin (G), Analytics (H), and Company (J) are not report sections.

questions.stem: Which tool is used to define relationships between fields in an import set table and a target table?
questions.explanation: A Transform Map defines relationships between fields in an import set table and a target table. It specifies how source columns map to target table fields during the import process. Schema Maps (B) show database structure, Dictionary Maps (C) don't exist, and Transform Schema (A) is not the correct term.
