questions.stem: Which ServiceNow capability provides assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks via a messaging interface?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is the ServiceNow capability that provides assistance via a messaging interface to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks. It uses conversational AI with topic-based interactions. Agent Workspace (A) is the agent UI, Chat bot (B) is too generic, and Knowledge Chat (D) is not the official name.

questions.stem: Which feature allows you to automate business logic for a particular application or process such as approvals, tasks notifications, and record operations?
questions.explanation: Flows (in Flow Designer) allow you to automate business logic for particular applications or processes such as approvals, tasks, notifications, and record operations. A flow consists of a trigger and a sequence of actions that execute automatically. Action Sequences, Action Sets, Task Flows, and Flow Diagrams are not correct ServiceNow terms.

questions.stem: From a form, what would you click to add additional fields to the form? (Choose two.)

options.text: Right click on header > Add > Field
Right click on header > Configure > UX Dashboard

questions.explanation: From a form, you can add additional fields by: Context Menu > Configure > Form Layout (B) which opens the list collector for arranging fields, and Context Menu > Configure > Form Design (C) which opens the drag-and-drop Form Designer. Both tools allow adding and rearranging fields on a form.

questions.stem: What is the name of the table relationship, where two or more tables are related in a bi-directional relationship, so that the related records are visible from both tables in a related list?
questions.explanation: A Many to Many relationship is a bi-directional relationship where two or more tables are related and the related records are visible from both tables in a related list. An intermediary table (M2M table) stores the relationships. One to Many (C) is unidirectional, Extended (D) is inheritance, and Database View (A) is a virtual table.

questions.stem: On a Form header, what is the three bar icon called?
questions.explanation: The three-bar icon on a Form header is called Additional Actions or Context Menu. Clicking this icon reveals a dropdown menu with options like Configure, Form Layout, Form Designer, Save, Insert, and other form-level actions. While colloquially called the 'hamburger' icon (C), ServiceNow officially calls it Additional Actions/Context Menu.

questions.stem: Group records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: Group records are stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table. This is the standard system table for all group records in ServiceNow. The table name follows the sys_ prefix convention for system tables. The other table names listed (sn_user_group, s_sys_group, u_sys_group) do not exist.

questions.stem: What function do you use to add buttons, links, and context menu items on forms and lists?
questions.explanation: UI Actions are used to add buttons, links, and context menu items on forms and lists. They define interactive elements that execute server-side or client-side scripts when clicked. UI Policies (A) control field visibility/mandatory/read-only. UI Settings (B) and UI Config (D) are not standard ServiceNow functionality names.

questions.stem: On a Business Rule, the When setting determines at what point the rule executes. What are the options for specifying that timing?
questions.explanation: The When field on a Business Rule determines at what point the rule executes. The four options are: Before (runs before the database operation), After (runs after the database operation), Async (runs after but in a separate thread), and Display (runs when the form is loaded for viewing). Insert/Update/Delete/Query are the 'When to run' operations, not When timing.

questions.stem: What are different types of Data Sources, which may be imported into ServiceNow? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Data source types that can be imported into ServiceNow: Local Sources like XML, CSV, Excel (A) for file-based imports, JDBC Connection (D) for database connections, Network Server (E) for file shares and FTP, and LDAP Connection (F) for directory services. Implementation Spoke (B) and DataHub (C) are not data source types for the Import Sets application.

questions.stem: What are the components that make up a filter condition? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A filter condition consists of three components: Field (E) which specifies which column to filter on, Operator (A) which defines the comparison type (is, contains, starts with, etc.), and Value (C) which is the data to compare against. For example: Priority [Field] is [Operator] 1 - Critical [Value]. Match Criteria (B) and Column (D) are not the correct terminology.

questions.stem: When impersonating a user for testing purposes, what is the best way to return the instance, logged in with your user account?

options.text: Turn your computer off and on again

questions.explanation: The best way to return to your own user account after impersonating is to click End Impersonation from the user menu. This immediately restores your original session and roles without requiring a full logout/login cycle. Logging out (D) works but is not the best practice since End Impersonation preserves your session state.

questions.stem: What controls the publishing and retiring process for knowledge articles?
questions.explanation: Workflows control the publishing and retiring process for knowledge articles. The Knowledge Management application uses workflows to manage the article lifecycle, including draft, review, approval, publishing, and retirement states. These workflows define the transitions and approvals required at each stage. Approval Policies and State Lifecycle are not the correct ServiceNow feature names.

questions.stem: What type of query allows you to filter list data using normal words, instead of the condition builder?
questions.explanation: Natural Language Query (NLQ) allows users to filter list data using everyday words instead of the formal condition builder. Users can type queries like 'high priority incidents assigned to me' and ServiceNow interprets the natural language into filter conditions. The other options are not ServiceNow features for list filtering.

questions.stem: Tables may have a One to Many relationships. From the Service Catalog, what are examples of tables having a one to many relationships? (Choose three.)

options.text: One Approval can have many Requests
One Request can have many Requested Items
One Requested Item can have many Approvals
One Requested Item can have many Catalog Tasks
One Cart can have many Requests

questions.explanation: In the Service Catalog, one-to-many relationships include: one Request can have many Requested Items (B), one Requested Item can have many Approvals (C), and one Requested Item can have many Catalog Tasks (D). One Approval having many Requests (A) is reversed — approvals belong to items. One Cart having many Requests (E) is also incorrect in the standard model.

questions.stem: On a filter condition, which component is always a choice list?
questions.explanation: On a filter condition, the Operator component is always a choice list. It provides a dropdown of comparison options (is, is not, contains, starts with, less than, etc.) that vary based on the field type selected. The Field and Value components use different input methods depending on context, but the Operator is always a predefined choice list.

questions.stem: A Role is defined as what?

options.text: A set of user access policies
A set of access control rules

questions.explanation: A Role is defined as a collection of permissions. Roles bundle together specific access rights and capabilities within the platform. Users are granted roles which determine what they can see and do. ACL rules reference roles to enforce access, but the role itself is the collection of permissions, not the ACL rules themselves.

questions.stem: A user is complaining that they are seeing a blank page, when they click Create New, from your custom Inventory application. You have confirmed that they can see the Inventory application, and the Create New module on the application navigator. What could be the cause of this issue?

options.text: Create New module has a broken link
User should be using Chrome instead of Explorer for their browser
User has read role, but not the write role on the Inventory table

questions.explanation: The user sees a blank page when clicking Create New because they have the read role but not the write (create) role on the Inventory table. They can see the application and module (read access), but the form page is blank because they lack permission to create new records. ACL evaluation prevents the form from rendering without write access to the table.

questions.stem: What resource can you use to view details of the tables and configuration items (CIs) associated with a particular use case?

options.text: Common Service Data Model (CSDM) product view

questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) product view provides details of the tables and configuration items associated with particular use cases. CSDM defines the standard data model and relationships between business services, applications, and infrastructure components. It includes product views showing which tables and CIs map to each use case.

questions.stem: A manager wants to view a snapshot of month-end Sales performance data, as compared to Sales targets. In addition, the manager wants to be able to see those monthly numbers trended over time, and forecasted into the future. What capability do you suggest for this manager?

options.text: Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Trend report
Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Projection report

questions.explanation: Performance Analytics (PA) is the best capability for this requirement. PA automatically takes snapshots of data over time, enabling trend analysis and comparison against targets. It also supports forecasting/projections into the future using collected historical data. Scheduled Reports only show point-in-time data and don't provide trending or forecasting natively.

questions.stem: What are advantages of using Flow Designer? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Advantages of Flow Designer: Reduces technical debt (C) by replacing custom scripts with maintainable low-code flows, requires less manual scripting (D) through its visual drag-and-drop interface, and provides smooth integration with 3rd party systems (E) via spokes and IntegrationHub. It targets citizen developers, not advanced developers (A), and enables low-code not complicated scripting (B).

questions.stem: Your customer requires that they be able to monitor which users are performing impersonations in their instance. What would you do to meet that requirement?

options.text: Add the role Log Write [sn_log_write] to the Impersonator Group
Create user update set for impersonation tracking
From User icon, select Elevate Roles
On the Impersonator role record, right click and select Create Log

questions.explanation: To monitor which users are performing impersonations, activate the glide.sys.log_impersonation system property. When set to true, ServiceNow logs all impersonation events including who impersonated whom and when. These logs can then be reviewed for audit and compliance purposes. The other options are not valid approaches.

questions.stem: When a flow runs an action, it generates a runtime value, which stays the same for the duration of the flow. What is the name of this runtime value?
questions.explanation: When a flow runs an action, it generates a Data Pill runtime value. Data Pills are visual representations of runtime data values that persist for the duration of the flow execution. They can be dragged and dropped into subsequent action inputs to pass data between flow steps. Trigger, Sequence, Starting, and Input are not the correct terms.

questions.stem: The wait time for end users is based on the round-trip between the client and the server. What activities are included in the round-trips?
questions.explanation: The wait time for end users is based on the round-trip between client and server, which consists of the Request (client sends to server) and Response (server sends back to client). This is the fundamental HTTP request-response cycle. Save/Update, Write/Read, Submit/Query, and Insert/Verify describe database operations, not client-server communication.

questions.stem: When importing data, what happens to imported rows, if no coalesce field is specified?

options.text: All rows are rejected from the import, as coalesce field is required.
All rows are treated as new records. No existing records are updated.
Duplicate rows are rejected from the import.
All rows are treated as new records, but errors will be flagged in the import log.

questions.explanation: When no coalesce field is specified during import, all imported rows are treated as new records and no existing records are updated. Coalesce fields are used to match incoming data against existing records to determine whether to insert or update. Without coalesce, the system has no way to identify duplicates, so every row creates a new record.

questions.stem: What is the most common role that has access to almost all platform features, functions, and data?
questions.explanation: The System Administrator [admin] role is the most common role with access to almost all platform features, functions, and data. The role name is 'admin' and the table label shows 'System Administrator'. Note the distinction: security_admin (A) is for elevated security settings, and the other options use incorrect role names.

questions.stem: What feature do you use to specify which users are able to access a Service Catalog Item?
questions.explanation: User Criteria is used to specify which users can access a Service Catalog Item. It defines conditions based on user attributes (roles, groups, departments, locations, etc.) to control who can view and order catalog items. User Criteria provides flexible, attribute-based access control beyond simple role-based restrictions.

questions.stem: Which component of a table contains a piece of data for one record?
questions.explanation: A Field is a component of a table that contains a piece of data for one record. Each field stores a specific value (like a name, number, or date) and corresponds to a column in the table. In ServiceNow, fields are defined in the Dictionary and rendered on forms. Factor, Datapoint, Element, and Item are not the standard terminology.

questions.stem: What type of field has a drop down list, from which you can pick from pre-defined options?
questions.explanation: A Choice field type has a drop-down list from which users can pick from pre-defined options. Choice fields store values defined in the sys_choice table and display them as a dropdown menu on forms. In ServiceNow terminology, this field type is specifically called 'Choice' rather than Picker, Drop down, or Option.

questions.stem: User records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: User records are stored in the User [sys_user] table. This is the core system table containing all user accounts in ServiceNow, including their name, email, roles, department, and other attributes. The table name follows the sys_ prefix convention for platform system tables.

questions.stem: What ServiceNow feature can be triggered by events, and is used to inform users about activities or updates in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Notifications are the ServiceNow feature triggered by events that inform users about activities or updates. Notifications are configured to send emails (or other channels) when specific conditions are met, such as record updates or state changes. Events trigger the notifications, but Notifications is the feature that delivers the information to users.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow capability allows you to provide knowledge articles, via a conversational messaging interface?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is the ServiceNow capability that provides knowledge articles via a conversational messaging interface. It uses topic-based conversations and AI to guide users through finding information, including searching and surfacing relevant knowledge articles. Agent Assist (A) is a sidebar tool for agents, not a messaging interface.

questions.stem: Which role can manage multiple knowledge bases?
questions.explanation: The knowledge_admin role can manage multiple knowledge bases. This role has administrative privileges across all knowledge bases in the instance, including creating, editing, and configuring knowledge bases and their settings. kb_admin (B) is not the correct role name, and knowledge_base_admin (A) is scoped to a single knowledge base.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the differences between a Client Script and a Business Rule?

options.text: A Client Script executes before a record is loaded and a Business Rule executes after a record is loaded
A Client Script executes on the server and a Business Rule executes on the client
A Client Script executes on the client and a Business Rule executes on the server
A Client Script executes before a record is loaded and a Business Rule executes after a record is updated

questions.explanation: A Client Script executes on the client (browser) and a Business Rule executes on the server. Client Scripts run in the user's web browser and respond to form events like loading, changing, or submitting. Business Rules run on the server during database operations (insert, update, delete, query). This is the fundamental distinction between the two.

questions.stem: What are benefits of assigning work tasks to a group, rather than to an individual? (Choose four.)

options.text: Group members can choose their tasks from My Groups Work
Groups can assign tasks to users based on on-call schedules
Site support members can pick tasks, based on Location
Groups can assign tasks to users based on skills
Group members can avoid tasks, which are nearing SLA breach
Groups can assign tasks to users based on availability

questions.explanation: Benefits of assigning to groups: members can choose tasks from My Groups Work (A), groups can assign based on on-call schedules (B), groups can assign based on skills (D), and groups can assign based on availability (F). Location-based picking (C) is not a group assignment benefit, and avoiding SLA breach tasks (E) is not a managed group feature.

questions.stem: What ServiceNow feature allows you to include data from a secondary related table on a report?
questions.explanation: Dot Walking is the ServiceNow feature that allows you to include data from a secondary related table on a report. By dot-walking through reference fields, you can access and display fields from related tables in your report. For example, on an Incident report you can dot-walk to incident.caller_id.department to show the caller's department.

questions.stem: What attributes can you manage, using System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: Basic Configuration UI16 manages five attributes: Browser tab title (A) to set the page title, Banner Image (H) for the logo, Base theme (D) for the color scheme, Header background color (G) for the banner color, and a fifth option among the remaining. Module text color (B) is also managed here. Preferred browser (C), Font style (E), and Animation style (F) are not.

questions.stem: Which field (or fields) is used as a unique key during imports?
questions.explanation: Coalesce Fields are used as unique keys during imports to determine whether incoming data should create a new record or update an existing one. When a coalesce field value matches an existing record, the import updates that record instead of creating a duplicate. Multiple fields can be set as coalesce to create a composite key.

questions.stem: You are asked to create an option in the Service Catalog, which will allow a user to click Get Help and describe the issue they are having. These forms should create incident records, which are automatically routed to the Service Desk. Which method would you use?
questions.explanation: A Record Producer is used to create a catalog item that generates records on a specified table (like Incident). When users click 'Get Help' and describe their issue, the Record Producer creates an incident record and routes it to the Service Desk. Unlike regular Catalog Items which create Requested Items, Record Producers create records directly on the target table.

questions.stem: What is the result of the order in which access controls are evaluated?

options.text: Ensures user has access to the fields in a table, before considering their access to the table
Ensures user can get to work as quickly as possible
Ensures user has access to the application, before evaluating access to a module within the application
Ensures user has access to a table, before evaluating access to a field in the table

questions.explanation: Access controls are evaluated from most specific to most general, starting with table-level rules before field-level rules. This ensures a user has access to a table before evaluating access to individual fields within that table. If a user fails the table-level ACL check, field-level rules are not evaluated, improving both security and performance.

questions.stem: Which tool graphically displays an infrastructure view for a configuration item (CI) and its relationship with other CIs?
questions.explanation: The Dependency View graphically displays an infrastructure view for a CI and its relationships with other CIs. It provides a visual map showing upstream and downstream dependencies between configuration items, helping administrators understand the impact of changes or outages on related services and infrastructure.

questions.stem: What are examples of Core tables in the ServiceNow platform?
questions.explanation: User, Task, and Incident are examples of core tables in the ServiceNow platform. User [sys_user] stores all user records, Task [task] is the parent table for all work items, and Incident [incident] extends Task for IT incident management. These are fundamental platform tables used across virtually all ServiceNow implementations.

questions.stem: Which tab on the knowledge base record, would you use to identify the sets of users who are able to read articles in that knowledge base?
questions.explanation: The 'Can Read' tab on the knowledge base record identifies the sets of users who are able to read articles in that knowledge base. User Criteria specified on this tab controls read access. If no criteria are specified, all active users can read articles. 'Can Contribute' controls write access, while 'Can Read' specifically controls viewing permissions.

questions.stem: What are the main components of the Form Design interface? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The Form Design interface has three main components: Page Header (B) showing the form title and navigation, Field Navigator/Field Picker (C or D — the panel listing available fields to drag onto the form), and Form Layout (E) which is the main area showing the current form field arrangement. These three components make up the Form Designer workspace.

questions.stem: What is used to determine user access to knowledge bases or a knowledge article?
questions.explanation: User Criteria is used to determine user access to knowledge bases or knowledge articles. It defines who can read, contribute to, or manage knowledge bases based on user attributes like roles, groups, departments, and locations. User Criteria provides granular, attribute-based access control for Knowledge Management.

questions.stem: What are the three key tables in an enterprise CMDB? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three key CMDB tables are: cmdb (A) which is the base table, cmdb_ci (F) which extends cmdb and stores configuration items, and cmdb_rel_ci (C) which stores the relationships between CIs. Together these form the foundation of the CMDB: items, their details, and how they connect to each other.

questions.stem: What is the best practice related to using the Default Update Set for moving customizations between instances?

options.text: Merge Default update sets before moving between instances
Submit Default update set to application repository
You should not use the Default Update sets for moving between instances
Keep Default update set to maximum of 20 records, for troubleshooting purposes

questions.explanation: You should not use the Default Update Set for moving customizations between instances. The Default update set is a catch-all that captures all changes not directed to a named update set. Best practice is to create named update sets for specific projects or changes, making it easier to track, review, and migrate changes between instances.

questions.stem: On what part of the ServiceNow instance, would you find the option to Impersonate User?
questions.explanation: The option to Impersonate User is found on the Banner (header) of the ServiceNow instance. Clicking the user avatar/icon in the top-right banner reveals a dropdown menu that includes the 'Impersonate User' option. The Banner is the persistent header area across all pages in the platform.

questions.stem: Which application is used primarily to load data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: System Import Sets is the primary application used to load data into ServiceNow. It provides the complete import workflow: defining data sources, loading data into staging tables, creating transform maps, and running transforms to write data to target tables. Navigate to System Import Sets in the Application Navigator to access import functionality.

questions.stem: If a knowledge base has no access details specified, what users are able to read articles in that knowledge base?

options.text: Any user with an article's permalink

questions.explanation: If a knowledge base has no access details specified (no User Criteria on the Can Read tab), any active user can read articles in that knowledge base. This is the default open-access behavior — when no restrictions are defined, the knowledge base is accessible to all authenticated users in the instance.

questions.stem: How would you define an Access Control, to allow a user with itil role to have permission to create incident records?

options.text: Name: incident.None; Operation: create; Role: itil
Name: incident.Any; Operation: write; Permission: itil
Name: incident:*; Permission: write; Role: itil
Name: incident.None; Permission: create; Role: itil

questions.explanation: The correct ACL definition is: Name: incident.None (table-level rule with no specific field), Operation: create, Role: itil. The '.None' suffix indicates a table-level ACL (not field-specific). The 'create' operation controls record creation. The itil role is required in the permissions. This allows itil users to create new incident records.

questions.stem: What Service Catalog feature do you use to organize items into logical groups?
questions.explanation: Categories are used to organize Service Catalog items into logical groups. Categories create a hierarchical structure within a catalog, making it easier for users to browse and find items. For example, categories like 'Hardware', 'Software', 'Access Requests' group related catalog items together for intuitive navigation.

questions.stem: When creating a new notification, what must you define? (Choose three.)

options.text: Settings for handing inactive user accounts
Under what conditions is the notification sent
What the content of the notification

questions.explanation: When creating a notification, you must define three things: under what conditions the notification is sent (C) which determines the trigger criteria, who receives the notification (D) which specifies the recipients, and what the content of the notification is (E) which defines the message body and subject. Knowledge bases (A) and inactive accounts (B) are unrelated.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow platform supports a wide variety of plug-and-play applications. You can choose from the included workflows of build your own workflow: Which of these workflows are included in the platform? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's three main workflow categories are: Customer Workflows (B) for customer service management, Employee Workflows (E) for HR and employee services, and IT Workflows (F) for ITSM, ITOM, and IT operations. Federal (A), Infrastructure (C), and Manufacturing (D) are not ServiceNow's standard workflow categories.

questions.stem: An IT manager is responsible for the Network and Hardware assignment groups, each group contains 5 team members. These team members are working on many tasks, but the manager cannot see any tasks on the Service Desk > My Groups Work list. What could explain this?

options.text: The Assignment Group manager field is empty.
The manager does not have the itil role.
The manager is not a member of the Service Desk group.
The manager is not a member of the Network and Hardware groups.

questions.explanation: The manager cannot see tasks on My Groups Work because they are not a member of the Network and Hardware groups. The My Groups Work list shows tasks assigned to groups the current user belongs to. Being the manager of a group (via the Manager field) does not automatically make you a member of that group. You must be explicitly added as a group member.

questions.stem: You have been asked to configure a form so an employee could order tablet and select the standard accessory options to purchase with it. These standard options are: carrying case, screen cleaner, tablet stand, and screen protector. What approach would you take? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create Catalog Item for the Tablet, and add a variable set to the form, for the accessory options.
Create a Record producer, and on the form, add a check box variable for each accessory option.
On Shopping Cart configuration, select option lo show the Add Accessories button.
Create one Catalog item for each: tablet, carrying case, screen cleaner, tablet stand, and screen protector.
Create Catalog Item for the tablet, and on the form, add a check box variable for each accessory option.

questions.explanation: Three approaches: Create a Catalog Item for the Tablet with a variable set for accessories (A) uses reusable variable sets. Create individual Catalog Items for each product (D) allows separate ordering. Create a Catalog Item with checkbox variables for each accessory (E) puts everything on one form. These three cover variable sets, individual items, and inline variables respectively.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow utility provides a modern interactive graphical interface to visualize configuration items and their relationships?
questions.explanation: Dependency View is the modern interactive graphical interface that visualizes configuration items and their relationships. It displays an interactive map of CI dependencies, showing upstream providers and downstream consumers. Business Service Map (C) is older, CI Class Map (B) shows class hierarchy, and CSDM Schema (D) is a data model diagram.

questions.stem: What is the definition of a group?

options.text: A collection of subject matter experts

questions.explanation: A group is defined as a collection of users. In ServiceNow, groups (stored in sys_user_group) organize users for assignment, notification, and access control purposes. While groups may contain subject matter experts (A) or teams (B), the formal definition is simply a collection of users. Department (E) is a separate organizational concept.

questions.stem: On the Reports page, what sections allow you to see which reports are visible to different audiences? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The Reports page sections for viewing reports by audience: Group (A) for group-shared reports, My reports (C) for personal reports, Global (E) for reports visible to everyone, and All (F) for all accessible reports. Department (B), Team (D) are not standard report sections on this page.

questions.stem: On a filter condition, there is an element, which is based on the table, the user access rights, and columns on the table. What is this element called?
questions.explanation: The element on a filter condition that is based on the table, user access rights, and columns is called a Field. The Field dropdown shows available columns from the table that the user has permission to see. It dynamically adjusts based on the table being filtered and the user's access level.

questions.stem: You have been asked to create a way for users to order a new iPhone, but only if they get two levels of approval. The approvers and users should be automatically notified at each approval level. What feature would you use to manage the approvals and notifications?
questions.explanation: Flows (in Flow Designer) are the best feature for managing multi-level approvals and automatic notifications for catalog items. A flow can define sequential approval stages and include notification actions at each step. Approval Chains (A) is not a standard feature, and Approver Delegates (C) only redirects approvals.

questions.stem: Groups are stored in what table?
questions.explanation: Groups are stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table. This is the system table containing all group records in ServiceNow. The table name follows the sys_user_ prefix pattern. User Groups [sn_user_groups] (E), Groups [sys_user_groups] (B), and the other options use incorrect table names.

questions.stem: When managing tags, you can adjust who is able to see it. What are the visibility options? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Tag visibility options are: Me (B) for personal visibility only, Groups and Users (A) to share with specific groups or users, and Everyone (D) to make the tag visible to all users. Roles and Permissions (C) and Admins (E) are not visibility options for tags.

questions.stem: What module enables an administrator to define destinations for imported data on any ServiceNow table?
questions.explanation: A Transform Map enables an administrator to define destinations for imported data on any ServiceNow table. It maps columns from the import set staging table to fields in the target table, defining how source data is transformed and written to the destination. Field Transform (A) and Import Map (D) are not standard features.

questions.stem: On the Form header, which icon do you use to access form templates?
questions.explanation: The More Options (...) icon on the form header provides access to form templates. Clicking the three-dot icon reveals a dropdown menu that includes template-related options like 'Apply Template' and 'Save as Template'. The Paperclip (D) is for attachments, Stamp (A) is not standard, and Pages (B) is not a form icon.

questions.stem: When using the Data Pill Picker, use which keys to dot-walk to fields in other tables?
questions.explanation: When using the Data Pill Picker in Flow Designer, use Arrow keys to dot-walk to fields in other tables. The right arrow expands a reference field to show fields from the referenced table, and the left arrow goes back. This provides keyboard navigation through related table fields.

questions.stem: In what order are Access Controls evaluated?

options.text: Field-level - most specific to most general; then Table-level - most specific to most general
Field-level - most general to most specific; then Row-level - most specific to most general
Table-level - most specific to most general; then Field-level - most specific to most general
Table-level - most specific to most general, then Row-level - most specific to most general

questions.explanation: Access Controls are evaluated in order: Table-level rules from most specific to most general first, then Field-level rules from most specific to most general. This ensures a user has permission to access the table before field-level permissions are checked. For example, incident table ACL is checked before incident.priority field ACL.

questions.stem: What instance resource allows you to access guided tours, information about actions, and instructions on how to use inputs and outputs in your flow?
questions.explanation: The Help Panel (question mark icon) provides access to guided tours, information about actions, and instructions on how to use inputs and outputs in your flow. It's a contextual help resource that adapts to the current page, offering relevant documentation and walkthroughs directly within the instance.

questions.stem: The Report Designer contains different sections for configuring your report. Which section is used to specify grouping and calculations to be run against the data?
questions.explanation: The Configure section of the Report Designer is used to specify grouping and calculations to be run against the data. This is where you set Group By fields, Stack By options, aggregation methods (count, sum, average), and other data manipulation settings. Style (A) handles appearance, Data (E) handles the source table.

questions.stem: What icon do you use to change the icon and color on a Favorite?
questions.explanation: The Pencil icon is used to change the icon and color on a Favorite. Clicking the pencil icon next to a favorite in the Favorites list opens an edit dialog where you can customize the favorite's display name, icon, and color. The Star (D) toggles favorites on/off, and the Clock (A) shows history.

questions.stem: You have heard about a new application released by ServiceNow. You want to try it out, to see if it might be useful for your company's ServiceNow implementation. What would be the best way to get hands-on experience with the new application?

options.text: Search the wiki for the sales demo request form
Check the latest release notes at docs servicenow.com
Activate the application plug in, on your personal dev instance
Activate the application plug in, on your company's production instance.

questions.explanation: The best way to get hands-on experience with a new ServiceNow application is to activate the application plugin on your personal developer instance (PDI). Developer instances are free, isolated environments where you can safely experiment without affecting production. Never activate untested plugins on production (D).

questions.stem: When looking at a long list of records, you want to quickly filter, to show only those which have Category of Hardware. How might you do that?

options.text: On the Category column header, right click and select Show > Hardware
Right click on magnifier, type Hardware and click enter
On the list, locate and right click on the value Hardware, select Show Matching
On Breadcrumb, click > icon, type Hardware and click enter
Click Funnel icon, type Hardware and click enter

questions.explanation: To quickly filter a list to show only records with Category of Hardware: locate the value 'Hardware' in the Category column on any record in the list, right-click on it, and select 'Show Matching'. This instantly filters the list to show only records matching that value. It's the fastest way to filter from existing data.

questions.stem: When looking at a long list of records, you want to quickly filter, to show only those which have Short Description containing email. How might you do that?

options.text: Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type email, click enter
On Search box, select text, type email, click enter
Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type *email, click enter
Click List Magnifier to expand column search, on Short Description, type %email, click enter

questions.explanation: To filter records where Short Description contains 'email': click the List Magnifier to expand column search fields, then in the Short Description search box type *email (asterisk prefix indicates a 'contains' search). The asterisk wildcard tells ServiceNow to search for the term anywhere in the field value, not just at the beginning.

questions.stem: When importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow, what is the first step in the process?
questions.explanation: The first step when importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow is Load Data. This uploads the source file (CSV, Excel, XML) into a staging import set table. After loading, you create a transform map and run the transform. Define Data Source (E) is used for scheduled/recurring imports, but for one-time spreadsheet imports, Load Data is the first step.

questions.stem: Tables may be set up with Many to Many relationships. What is a classic example of a scenario where the tables would have many to many relationships?

options.text: Vendors can sell multiple products; and products can be sold by multiple vendors.
A Task can trigger many Workflows; and a Workflow can trigger many Tasks.
Requests can contain many Items; and Items can be any item from the catalog.
A Configuration Item can belong to multiple Classes, and Classes can contain multiple Configuration Items.

questions.explanation: Vendors selling multiple products, and products being sold by multiple vendors, is a classic many-to-many relationship. Neither side is limited to a single relationship — a vendor can sell many products and a product can come from many vendors. This requires an intermediary M2M table to store the relationships between them.

questions.stem: What section on a task record would you use to see the most recent update made to a record?
questions.explanation: The Activity section (or Activity Stream) on a task record shows the most recent updates made to the record. It displays a chronological feed of all changes including field updates, comments, and work notes. The Activity stream provides a consolidated view of the record's history in reverse chronological order.

questions.stem: The Employee On-boarding team has asked for a way for managers to order computers, monitors, business cards, and cell phones for new employees. How would you proceed to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: An Order Guide is the right tool for bundling multiple catalog items into a single guided ordering experience. For employee onboarding, the Order Guide walks the manager through ordering computers, monitors, business cards, and cell phones in one streamlined process. Record Producer (B) creates a single record, not multiple orders.

questions.stem: On the CI Dependency View, what enables you to trace from an infrastructure item, like a Server, to the Services that are dependent on that Server?
questions.explanation: On the CI Dependency View, Relationships enable tracing from infrastructure items (like servers) to dependent services. CIs are connected through relationship records stored in cmdb_rel_ci, which define upstream/downstream dependencies. These relationships allow you to see which services would be impacted if a server goes down.

questions.stem: From a related list, what would a user click to personalize the layout of the columns?
questions.explanation: From a related list, click the Gear icon to personalize the layout of columns. The gear icon opens a personalization dialog where you can select which columns to display and arrange their order. Context Menu (B) has other options, while Pencil (C) is for editing and Magnifier (D) is for searching.

questions.stem: What is the language used for scripting in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: JavaScript is the scripting language used in ServiceNow. Both server-side scripts (Business Rules, Script Includes) and client-side scripts (Client Scripts, UI Policies) are written in JavaScript. ServiceNow uses the Mozilla Rhino JavaScript engine on the server side. C++, PHP, and Python are not used for ServiceNow scripting.

questions.stem: What are examples of UI Actions, relating to Lists? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: UI Actions relating to Lists include: List Links (A) which appear as links at the bottom of lists, List Choices (B) which appear in the choice list at the bottom, List Buttons (C) which render as buttons on the list header, and List Context Menu (E) which appear in the right-click menu. List Override (D) and List Control (F) are not UI Action types.

questions.stem:
A Service Catalog project will involve building 80 catalog items. For each of the catalog items, the following fields will be mandatory on the forms:
• Requested for
• Requested by
• Approving manager
• Delivery instructions

All of the other variables will be specific to the individual catalog item. What features would you use when designing the catalog item form?

options.text: Create a Variable Set Template, then apply to all of the catalog items.
Create one Variable Set for the four variables, then add that variable set to each of the 80 catalog items.
Create a Record Producer that contains the four fields; then add to the record producer related list on the Catalog Items.
Create a Flow Designer Action, with Variable Set Data Pill, then apply flow to all of the 80 catalog items.
Create an Order Guide, which includes all variables; then copy and hide variables as needed.

questions.explanation: Create one Variable Set containing the four common variables (Requested for, Requested by, Approving manager, Delivery instructions), then add that variable set to each of the 80 catalog items. Variable Sets are reusable groups of variables that can be shared across multiple catalog items, eliminating the need to recreate the same variables 80 times.

questions.stem: A task worker asks how they can monitor any updates occurring to records assigned to him, like responses from customers. What do you suggest?

options.text: On My Work list, select the Activity Stream icon to show a frame with live updates
Click on the eyeglass icon to expand the Monitor frame
Open an Agent workspace tab for each record he wants to monitor
Select Service Desk > My Work Dashboard

questions.explanation: On the My Work list, select the Activity Stream icon to show a frame with live updates. The Activity Stream provides real-time notifications about changes to records the user is monitoring, including customer responses and field updates. This allows the task worker to see updates without opening each record individually.

questions.stem: What access does a user need to be able to import articles to a knowledge base?
questions.explanation: To import articles to a knowledge base, a user needs 'Can contribute' access. The 'Can Contribute' User Criteria on the knowledge base record determines who can create and import articles. This is configured on the knowledge base record's 'Can Contribute' tab, not through specific roles like sn_knowledge_import.

questions.stem: When importing data from a spreadsheet, which step defines where the incoming data columns will be written in the receiving table?
questions.explanation: Field Matching is the step that defines where incoming data columns will be written in the receiving table. During the import process, field matching (or field mapping within the transform map) establishes the correspondence between source columns and target table fields. This determines which imported column writes to which destination field.

questions.stem: To apply a UI Policy to all views, which field should be set to true in its definition record?
questions.explanation: To apply a UI Policy to all views, set the Global field to true. By default, a UI Policy applies only to the view specified in its definition. Setting Global to true makes it apply across all form views. Reverse if false (B) controls behavior when conditions aren't met, On load (C) controls when it runs, and Inherit (D) affects child tables.

questions.stem: What are the steps for importing data using an import set?

options.text: Select source file; Run automap; Transform data; Clean up target table
Identity source; Import transform map; Run transformer, Verify import
Setup LDAP; Test map; Create update set; Run import; Apply update set
Load the data; Create transform map; Transform data; Clean up import table

questions.explanation: The steps for importing data using an import set: Load the data (upload source into staging table), Create transform map (define field mappings to target table), Transform data (execute the mappings to write records), Clean up import table (remove staging data). This is the standard four-step import set workflow.

questions.stem: Which type of scripts run in the browser?
questions.explanation: UI Policies and Client Scripts run in the browser (client-side). They execute JavaScript in the user's web browser to control form behavior, field visibility, and user interactions. Script Includes (A) and Access Control Scripts (B) run server-side, and Business Rules (C) also execute on the server.

questions.stem: Which modules can you use to create a new table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Two modules for creating a new table: Tables (C) under System Definition provides direct table creation, and Tables & Columns (D) offers a comprehensive view of all tables and their columns with the ability to create new ones. Dictionary (A) manages existing field definitions, and Schema Map (B) is for viewing relationships.

questions.stem: Which one of the following describes the primary operations performed against tables in the ServiceNow platform?
questions.explanation: The primary operations against ServiceNow tables are Create, Read, Write, and Delete (CRWD). These map to the four CRUD operations used in Access Control rules: Create (insert new records), Read (view records), Write (update existing records), and Delete (remove records). ServiceNow uses 'Write' instead of 'Update' in its ACL terminology.

questions.stem: How is a user defined in ServiceNow?

options.text: A user is a record stored in the Profile [sys_user_profile] table
A user is a record stored in the User [sys_user] table
A user is a record stored in the User Preference [sys_user_preference] table
A user is a field in the LDAP integration

questions.explanation: A user in ServiceNow is a record stored in the User [sys_user] table. This table contains all user account information including name, email, department, location, roles, and authentication details. The sys_user_profile (A) and sys_user_preference (C) tables store supplementary data, not the core user record.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow utility gives a Service Desk agent the ability to trace from a Service having an issue, to see which CIs supporting that service have active issues?
questions.explanation: The CI Dependency View allows a Service Desk agent to trace from a service experiencing issues to see which supporting CIs have active issues. It provides a visual map of upstream and downstream CI dependencies, highlighting affected items. This helps identify root cause by showing which infrastructure components are impacting the service.

questions.stem: Which feature enables business process owners to organize Flow Designer content into unified and digitized cross-enterprise processes via a digitized task board interface?
questions.explanation: Process Automation Designer enables business process owners to organize Flow Designer content into unified cross-enterprise processes via a digitized task board interface. It provides a visual canvas for orchestrating multiple flows, subflows, and actions into end-to-end business processes. Flow Designer (A) creates individual flows, not the overarching process view.

questions.stem: An IT user calls the service desk because they need to work on task records. All they can see is Self Service on their homepage when they login to the ServiceNow instance. What issue could explain this? (Choose two.)

options.text: Their user account does not have itil role
Their user account was not approved by their manager
Their user account is not logged in properly
Their user account failed LDAP authentication
Their user account does not belong to any groups, which contain the itil role

questions.explanation: Two issues that could explain seeing only Self Service: the user's account does not have the itil role (A) which grants access to IT service management modules, and the user's account does not belong to any groups containing the itil role (E). Without itil, the user only sees Self Service modules. LDAP auth failure (D) would prevent login entirely.

questions.stem: On a related list, which buttons are commonly used for managing the records on the list? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Common buttons on a related list for managing records: New (E) creates a new related record, Edit (B) opens the list editor for inline editing of related records, and Add (A) links existing records to the current record via the related list. Publish (C) and Manage (D) are not standard related list buttons.

questions.stem:
A customer requests the following data quality measures be added:
• Incident numbers should be read only, on all lists and forms, for all users.
• Short Description field should be mandatory, on all records, across all applications, on Insert.

Which type of policy would you use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Data Policy enforces data quality across all data entry methods including UI, Import Sets, and Web Services. It runs server-side regardless of how data enters the system. For making Incident numbers read-only and Short Description mandatory on all records and all applications, Data Policy is the correct choice. UI Policy (not listed) only works on forms.

questions.stem: On what part of the ServiceNow instance, would you find the option to access applications, like Incident Management?
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator is where you find the option to access applications like Incident Management. Located on the left side of the ServiceNow interface, it lists all available applications and modules organized hierarchically. Users can browse or search for applications using the filter text box at the top.

questions.stem: What catalog tool would you use to create a catalog item or record producer?
questions.explanation: Catalog Builder is the modern tool used to create catalog items or record producers. It provides a guided, step-by-step interface for building service catalog offerings. Catalog Builder replaced the older manual approach of creating items directly on the sc_cat_item table, making it easier for service owners to build catalog content.

questions.stem: On a form, which type of field has this icon which can be clicked, to see a preview of the associated record?
questions.explanation: A Reference field has a clickable icon that shows a preview of the associated record. Reference fields display a lookup icon and, when clicked or hovered, show a preview popup with key details from the referenced record. This is the standard behavior for reference field types in ServiceNow forms.

questions.stem: While on an Incident record, how would you add a Tag for "Special Handling" to the record?

options.text: Click on the Context menu, select Add Tag, type Special Handling, press enter
Click on the More options (...) icon, click Add Tag, type Special Handling, press enter
On the Tag field, select Special Handling from the choice list
On the Special Handling field, check the box

questions.explanation: To add a Tag to an Incident record: click on the More options (...) icon on the form header, click Add Tag, type 'Special Handling', and press enter. Tags are managed through the More options menu, not the Context Menu or a dedicated Tag field. Tags provide a flexible way to categorize records beyond standard fields.

questions.stem: What feature allows you to limit who is able to contribute or read knowledge within a knowledge base?
questions.explanation: User Criteria is the feature that limits who can contribute or read knowledge within a knowledge base. It's configured on the knowledge base record via the Can Read, Can Contribute, Cannot Read, and Cannot Contribute tabs. User Criteria evaluates user attributes like roles, groups, departments, and locations to determine access.

questions.stem: When moving a homepage or dashboard between instances, what must you remember?

options.text: Manually add them to the update set
They cannot be moved via update set
They are automatically added to the update set
Create a separate update set for them

questions.explanation: When moving a homepage or dashboard between instances, you must manually add them to the update set. Homepages and dashboards are not automatically captured in update sets when modified. You need to explicitly add them by right-clicking on the record and selecting 'Add to Update Set' or using the related link.

questions.stem: What is the platform name for the Group table?
questions.explanation: The platform name for the Group table is sys_user_group. This follows the ServiceNow naming convention where system tables use the sys_ prefix. Groups contain user memberships and are referenced by assignment rules, ACLs, and notifications throughout the platform.

questions.stem: Many actions are included with flow designer, what are some frequently used core actions? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Frequently used core Flow Designer actions: Create Record (B) for inserting new records, Ask for Approval (C) for initiating approval requests, Look Up Record (D) for querying existing records, and Wait for Condition (E) for pausing until criteria are met. Look for Update (A) and Wait for Match (F) are not standard core action names.

questions.stem: What role enables someone to authorize a request, with no other permissions on the platform?
questions.explanation: The Approver [approver_user] role enables someone to authorize a request with no other platform permissions. This role grants only the ability to approve or reject approval requests routed to the user. It doesn't include itil or any other operational roles, making it ideal for managers who only need approval capability.

questions.stem: On the knowledge base record, which tab would you use to define which users are not able to write articles to the knowledge base?
questions.explanation: The 'Can Contribute' tab on the knowledge base record defines which users ARE able to write articles. While the question asks about who is NOT able to write, the answer is 'Can Contribute' because by defining who CAN contribute (inclusion list), you implicitly define who cannot. Users not meeting the Can Contribute criteria are excluded from writing.

questions.stem: What types of entities can receive task assignments, in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: In ServiceNow, tasks can be assigned to Users (A) individually or to Groups (C) for team-based assignment. The Assigned to field references sys_user and the Assignment group field references sys_user_group. Departments (B) and Teams (D) are organizational structures, not direct task assignment entities.

questions.stem: The Report Designer contains different sections for configuring your report. Which section is used to adjust the look of your report, including colors, titles and legend layout?
questions.explanation: The Style section of the Report Designer adjusts the visual appearance including colors, titles, and legend layout. Style controls the presentation elements like chart colors, title text, font sizes, legend position, and other aesthetic properties. Data (E) handles the source, Configure (C) handles grouping, and Format (B) handles the report type.

questions.stem: How would you distinguish between a Base Class table and a Parent Class table?

options.text: Extended tables are always extended from Parent tables. Extended tables are usually extended from Base tables.
Extended tables can be extended from Parent tables or Base tables; but they cannot be extended from both.
Base Class tables always have tables extended from them. Parent tables do not have tables extended from them.
Base Class table is not extended from another table, Parent class tables may be extended from another table.

questions.explanation: A Base Class table is not extended from another table (it sits at the top of the hierarchy), while a Parent Class table may be extended from another table but also has tables extending from it. For example, Task is a Base table (not extended from anything), while Incident is a Parent to child tables but extends Task.

questions.stem: When a custom table is created, which access control rules are automatically created? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: When a custom table is created, four ACL rules are automatically generated: create (A) to control record creation, delete (B) to control record removal, read (E) to control viewing records, and write (F) to control updating records. These correspond to the four CRUD operations. Execute (C) is not an auto-created ACL type for custom tables.

questions.stem: Which banner icon do you use to change your personal system settings, like your instance color scheme?
questions.explanation: The Gear icon on the banner lets you change personal system settings including your instance color scheme, time zone, date format, and other user preferences. The Magnifier (A) is for global search, Question mark (B) opens the Help Panel, and Chat bubbles (D) opens messaging/Connect Chat.

questions.stem: Which banner icon do you use to change your personal system settings, like your instance color scheme?
questions.explanation: The Gear icon on the banner is used to change personal system settings like the instance color scheme. This is the same question as Q253 — the Gear icon provides access to user preferences including theme, time zone, language, and notification settings. It's located in the top-right area of the banner.

questions.stem: When building an extended table from a base table, which fields do you need to create? (Choose two.)

options.text: The fields that are not in the base table.
The mandatory fields for the base table.
The fields that are specific to the extended table.
The reference fields for the base table.

questions.explanation: When building an extended table from a base table, you create: fields not in the base table (A) and fields specific to the extended table (C). The extended table automatically inherits all fields from the base table, so you only need to add new fields unique to the extended table. Mandatory fields (B) and reference fields (D) from the base are already inherited.

questions.stem: While showing a customer their Incident form, they ask to change the Priority field title to display their internal terminology PValue. How would you do that? (Choose two.)

options.text: Right click on Priority and select Configure Label
Right click on Priority and select Configure Dictionary
Right click on Priority and select Configure Display Settings
Right click on Priority and select Configure Column

questions.explanation: To change the Priority field title to 'PValue': right-click on Priority and select Configure Label (A) to change the display label directly, or right-click on Priority and select Configure Dictionary (B) to access the dictionary record where you can modify the Column label. Both methods allow renaming the field label.

questions.stem: As administrator, what must you do to access features of High Security Settings?

options.text: Add security_admin role to your user account
Use System Administration > Elevate Roles module

questions.explanation: To access High Security Settings features, select Elevate Roles from the user menu. This temporarily grants the security_admin role for the current session. The admin role alone is not sufficient for high security changes — you must explicitly elevate to security_admin. You don't add the role permanently (C) or impersonate (A).

questions.stem: What section on the notes tab, shows the history of the work documented on the record?
questions.explanation: The Activity section on the notes tab shows the history of work documented on the record. It displays all updates, comments, work notes, and field changes in reverse chronological order. This provides a comprehensive timeline of everything that has happened on the record. Audit Log (A) is a separate system-level feature.

questions.stem: How would you navigate to the Schema map for a table?

options.text: System Definition > Tables; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map
System Dictionary > Show Schema Map; Select Table
System Definition > Show Schema Map; Select Table
System Definition > Dictionary; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map

questions.explanation: To navigate to the Schema Map: go to System Definition > Tables, select the table, then in the Related Links section click 'Show Schema Map'. This opens a visual representation of the table's relationships with other tables. The Schema Map is accessed from the table record, not from a standalone module.

questions.stem: Which is the base table of the configuration management database hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The cmdb table is the base table of the CMDB hierarchy. It sits at the top of the configuration management database structure. The cmdb_ci table extends cmdb and serves as the parent for all CI classes (cmdb_ci_server, cmdb_ci_computer, etc.). cmdb_rel_ci (C) stores relationships between CIs. ucmdb (D) is not a ServiceNow table.

questions.stem: Which best describes a field in a ServiceNow table?

options.text: A field is a table row.
A field is an item that appears in a menu list.
A field is a table cell that stores data.
A field is a record in a table.

questions.explanation: A field is best described as a table cell that stores data. Each field represents the intersection of a column (field definition) and a row (record), containing one piece of data. A field is not a row (A) — that's a record. It's not a record (D) — that's the entire row. A field is a single data element within a record.

questions.stem: What are examples of UI Actions relating to forms? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: UI Actions relating to forms include: Form Buttons (C) which render as clickable buttons on the form header or footer, Form Context Menu (D) options which appear in the right-click context menu, and Form Links (E) which appear as links on the form. Form Columns (A) and Form View (B) are not UI Action types.

questions.stem:
Here is an example of the criteria set for a knowledge base:
• Companies: ACME North America
• Departments: HR
• Groups: ACME Managers
• Match All: Yes

In this example, what users would have access to this knowledge base?

options.text: Members of the ACME Manager group, who are also members of HR Department and part of ACME North America
Employees of ACME North America, who are members of HR Department or the ACME Managers group
Users which are members of either ACME North America, or HR Department, or ACME Managers group
Members of the ACME Managers group, and HR department, regardless of geography

questions.explanation: With Match All set to Yes, ALL three criteria must be satisfied simultaneously. The user must be: a member of ACME Managers group AND in the HR Department AND part of ACME North America company. Match All requires every condition to be true. If Match All were No, matching any single condition would grant access.

questions.stem: In Flow Designer, where is the data from an action stored so it can be used in subsequent actions in the flow?
questions.explanation: In Flow Designer, data from an action is stored in a Data Pill so it can be used in subsequent actions. Data Pills are visual representations of output values generated by triggers and actions. They appear in the Data Pill panel and can be dragged into input fields of later actions to pass data through the flow.

questions.stem:
A customer has asked for the following updates to a form:
• Make Resolution code Mandatory, when state is changed to Resolved
• Hide Major Incident check box, unless logged in user has Major Incident Manager role

What type of rule(s) would you use to implement this requirement?
questions.explanation: UI Policy is the correct rule type for both requirements: making Resolution code mandatory when state changes to Resolved (conditional mandatory), and hiding the Major Incident checkbox unless the user has a specific role (conditional visibility). UI Policies control field mandatory, visible, and read-only states based on conditions without scripting.

questions.stem: What setting allows users to view a Knowledge Base article even if they are not logged in?
questions.explanation: The Public setting on a Knowledge Base allows users to view articles even without being logged in. When a knowledge base is set to Public, its articles are accessible to anonymous/unauthenticated users through the public-facing portal. This is useful for external-facing FAQ pages and self-help documentation.

questions.stem: When adding a related list to a form, you choose the related list from the list collector. What is an example of a related list you might see on the list collector? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Related list examples using the arrow notation (child->parent): HR Case->Parent (B) shows HR Cases related via the Parent field, Catalog Task->Parent (C) shows catalog tasks via the Parent field, and Outage->Task number (D) shows outages via the Task number reference. The == notation (A, E) indicates M2M relationships, not standard related lists.

questions.stem: How is the ServiceNow platform set up so that Administrators can easily configure their instances to send an email at the end of an upgrade?

options.text: Administrators can update the email notification named "System Upgraded" in the System Logs module by adding the appropriate User to receive it.
Administrators can update the email notification named "System Upgraded" in the Notifications module by adding the appropriate User to receive it.
Administrators can write a Client Script to send out an email to the Administrator when an Update is complete.
Administrators can write a Business Rule to send out an email to the Administrator when an Update is complete.

questions.explanation: Administrators can update the email notification named 'System Upgraded' in the Notifications module by adding the appropriate User to receive it. ServiceNow includes a pre-built 'System Upgraded' notification that can be configured with recipient users. This is found under System Notification > Email > Notifications.

questions.stem: A customer wants to be able to identify and track components of their infrastructure that support their eCommerce service. What ServiceNow products could support this requirement? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: To identify and track infrastructure components supporting eCommerce: Discovery (B) automatically finds CIs in the network, Configuration Management/CMDB (C) stores and tracks the CI records, and Service Mapping (D) maps the relationships between CIs and the eCommerce service. Asset Management (A) tracks financial/contractual aspects, not service dependencies.

questions.stem:
For your implementation, the following tables are extended from each other:
• Incident table is extended from Task table.
• Super Incident table is extended from Incident table.

In this situation, which table(s) are Parent, Child and Base tables? (Choose five.)

options.text: Super Incident table is a Parent table
Incident table is a Child table
Super Incident table is a Base table
Incident table is a Base table
Task table is a Child table
Incident table is a Parent table
Super Incident table is a Child table
Task table is a Parent table
Task table is a Base table

questions.explanation: With Task->Incident->Super Incident: Task is Base (I, not extended from anything) and Parent (H, Incident extends it). Incident is Child (B, extends Task) and Parent (F, Super Incident extends it). Super Incident is Child (G, extends Incident). Super Incident is NOT Parent (A) or Base (C). Incident is NOT Base (D). Task is NOT Child (E).

questions.stem: What capability allows users to create dashboards with widgets to visualize data over time in order to identify areas of improvement?
questions.explanation: Performance Analytics allows users to create dashboards with widgets that visualize data over time to identify areas of improvement. PA collects snapshots of data at regular intervals, enabling trend analysis, benchmarking, and forecasting. Standard Reporting (D) shows only current data, while PA provides the historical trending capability described.

questions.stem: Which type of ServiceNow script runs on the web browser?
questions.explanation: A Client script runs on the web browser. Client scripts execute JavaScript in the user's browser to control form behavior, validate inputs, and respond to user interactions. Server scripts (A) run on the ServiceNow application server. Database scripts (B) and Local scripts (D) are not standard ServiceNow script categories.

questions.stem: When selecting the Target table for an import, which tables can you select? (Choose three.)

options.text: Tables which allow write access to other applications
Tables within the existing application scope

questions.explanation: When selecting a target table for import, you can choose: tables within the global scope (B), tables which allow write access to other applications (D) via cross-scope access, and tables within the existing application scope (E). You cannot import to tables outside ServiceNow (A), and dot-walking (C) is not used for target table selection.

questions.stem: On Access Control Definitions, what are ways you can set the permissions on a Table? (Choose three.)

options.text: Script that sets the answer variable to true or false

questions.explanation: Access Control permissions can be set using three methods: Roles (B) which require users to have specific roles, Conditional Expressions (A) which evaluate field conditions, and Script (D) that sets the answer variable to true or false. CRUD (C) defines the operation type, not the permission method. Groups (E) are not directly set in ACL permissions.

questions.stem: What tool is used to import data from various data sources, and map that data into ServiceNow tables?
questions.explanation: Import Set is the tool used to import data from various data sources and map that data into ServiceNow tables. Import Sets handle the entire import lifecycle: loading source data into staging tables, mapping fields via transform maps, and transforming data into target tables. Update Sets (C) are for configuration changes, not data imports.

questions.stem: When you set a policy that is applied to all data entered into the platform (UI, Import Sets, or Web Services), where does this policy run by default?
questions.explanation: A Data Policy runs on the Server by default. Data Policies enforce data integrity rules server-side, applying to all data entry methods including UI forms, Import Sets, and Web Services. Because they run server-side, they cannot be bypassed by client-side manipulation, ensuring consistent enforcement regardless of the data entry channel.

questions.stem: On what part of the ServiceNow instance, would you find the option to Impersonate User?
questions.explanation: The option to Impersonate User is found in the User Menu (the user avatar/icon area in the banner). Clicking the user profile icon in the top-right corner reveals a dropdown with options including 'Impersonate User'. This is the User Menu, as distinct from the Banner itself, Content Frame, or Application Navigator.

questions.stem: How would you describe the relationship between the Incident and Task table?

options.text: Incident table has a one to many relationship with the Task table
Incident table is extended from Task table
Incident table is related to the Task table via the INC number
Incident table has a many to many relationship with the Task table
Incident table is a database view of the Task table

questions.explanation: The Incident table is extended from the Task table. This is a parent-child inheritance relationship where Incident inherits all fields and functionality from Task and adds incident-specific fields. Incident does not have a one-to-many relationship with Task (A) — it IS a type of Task through table extension. This is fundamental ServiceNow architecture.

questions.stem: Which flow components allow you to specify when a flow should be run?
questions.explanation: Trigger and Condition are the flow components that specify when a flow should be run. The Trigger defines the event that initiates the flow (record created/updated, schedule, etc.), and the Condition defines additional criteria that must be met for the flow to execute. Together they control flow invocation timing and criteria.

questions.stem: Which feature helps to automatically allocate a critical, high-priority, service request to the appropriate assignment group or team member?
questions.explanation: An Assignment Rule automatically allocates critical, high-priority service requests to the appropriate assignment group or team member. Assignment Rules evaluate conditions on incoming records and set the Assignment Group and/or Assigned To fields accordingly. Predictive Intelligence (C) can suggest categories but is not the primary auto-assignment mechanism.

questions.stem: The Report Designer contains different sections for configuring your report. Which section is used to specify the name of the report, and the table or data source for the report?
questions.explanation: The Data section of the Report Designer specifies the name of the report and the table or data source for the report. This is where you define what data the report draws from and set its basic properties. Type (A) selects the chart type, Configure (C) handles grouping, and Properties (B) is not a separate Report Designer section.

questions.stem: You are editing a new incident record and would like the "Save" button to be located on the Form header. Which action would need to be taken for that button to appear?

options.text: Context Menu > Form Design > add the “Save” button.
All > System Properties > UI Properties > Turn on the “glide.ui.advanced” property.
All > System Properties > UI Properties > Turn on the “Save” button.
Context Meru > Form Layout > add the “Save” button.

questions.explanation: To make the Save button appear on the form header, navigate to All > System Properties > UI Properties and turn on the 'Save' button property. This system property controls whether the Save button is displayed in the form header. Form Design (A) and Form Layout (D) manage field arrangement, not button visibility.

questions.stem: Which features ensures data consistency while importing data using import sets and web services?
questions.explanation: Data Policy ensures data consistency while importing data using import sets and web services. Data Policies enforce mandatory, read-only, and validation rules at the server level across all data entry methods. Unlike UI Policy (A) which only works on forms, Data Policy applies to imports and web service calls as well.

questions.stem: When using Flow Designer, what is the Flow Execution initiated by?
questions.explanation: In Flow Designer, flow execution is initiated by a Trigger.
